Acceptance: Every section A-G is ticked or explicitly deferred with a reason, transcribed to config/gate-log.md under a slug-named heading (the J28 classifier reads the heading), and the gate's status flips from awaiting-sme. The six open questions Q0-Q6 are answered by the directory owner or recorded as still-open with the consequence of each stated. §G3 produces an explicit ruling on the K2 FID tier — it is a change to a SIGNED gate (seal-attribution-match-policy), so the outcome is either a recorded amendment to that gate or an explicit decision to leave the tier unfilled. Any vocabulary entry the gate confirms is registered status: planned (the K2 flips-are-follow-ups pattern) with its build groomed as a follow-up item; NO loader is built and NO pull is taken inside this item.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop). model: fable — this decides identity keys, edge meaning, and the correction of a signed gate. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN SCOPE: TierReconcilers.fid (drydocs/loaders/seal_attribution.py) has been an empty dict since the K2 build, so the signed precedence order SEAL > FID > APP_NAME > ALIAS has never had a working second tier. §G, added on live SME evidence 2026-08-05, is why this is not a simple "fill the table" job: a run-as account is REGISTERED to the platform application while its jobs are ATTRIBUTED elsewhere, so filling the tier as originally specified would resolve a job to the account's owning application and CONTRADICT a confirmed app-code mapping. The tier is harmless today only because the table is empty. TWO SME INPUTS RECORDED 2026-08-07 (laptop) — DIRECTION, NOT RULINGS. Neither ticks a clause; both constrain what the session may say, in the D3-SME-INPUT idiom G22 used. (1) EVERY FID CARRIES AT LEAST TWO HUMAN OWNERS. Three consequences. (a) The rule is a GRAPH TEST, never a constraint — minimum cardinality is not expressible in Neo4j, and the gate log already settled this twice ("NEVER a uniqueness constraint - graph-TEST instead (the TOM-roles lesson)"; "Neo4j cannot declare relationship cardinality any more than it could declare the TOM-roles singleton"). (b) IT HAS NOTHING TO ATTACH TO YET: doc 09's phase list models account -> APPLICATION (phase 4, BELONGS_TO_APPLICATION {role: service_account}) and NEVER account -> PERSON, so a rule about human owners has no edge. That gap is this gate's to rule, and it must not be swept into doc 09's standing deferral of CONTACT columns (support owners, teams, mailboxes -> email-dl-contact-point): owner-of-record is the accountability fact the directory exists to assert, not a contact point. (c) The census already MEASURES compliance — accounts_below_owner_minimum, kept separate from accounts_with_no_owner_recorded so an unmeasurable estate is never reported as a compliant one. (2) THE ORACLE TABLE IS AN ALTERNATIVE SOURCE FOR THE FID — and this is a THIRD answer to §Q3, which asks only "is the export the only pull mechanism, or is there an API?". Not an export, not an API: a replica already in scope whose confidential surface is already assessed. The distinction the session must hold: Oracle supplies the FID VALUE (CM_DEF_VJOB.OWNER, which the psgmgr ledger records as "run-as tenant Functional ID (service identity, not a person); also the :run_as scope-bind (exact match)"), but NOT the FID RECORD — it carries no type, no status and no application assignment, which are exactly the columns §D2's clause (c) breaks down by and Q0 compares against. So Oracle can source demand set (i); it CANNOT substitute for the directory extract, and if it did the census would report 100% coverage while measuring nothing. The upside worth recording: sourcing (i) from Oracle means the only thing crossing the boundary is the directory extract filtered to accounts already named, which is the smallest confidential surface available and is the argument doc 09 makes for demand-driven scope in the first place. SME INPUT (2) IS NOW PARTLY FALSIFIED — 2026-08-12, and the correction is the point. It recorded that Oracle supplies the FID VALUE but NOT the FID RECORD, because it 'carries no type, no status and no application assignment'. That is true of CM_DEF_VJOB — the Control-M job table — and was generalized from it to 'Oracle'. `psgmgr.HR_PHONE_EXP` carries ALL THREE: EMP_TYP_CD (type, 'FCT' for functional), EMP_STATUS_CD (status), CALC_LOB_NAME (LOB). So Oracle can source the RECORD as well as the value, the §D2 census runs inside one schema, and Q3 is answered with an option it did not offer. The half that still stands: the directory being reachable says nothing about whether its assignment AGREES with Control-M attribution — Q0/Q4 and the whole §G reading are untouched. THE account->PERSON GAP HAS A COLUMN NOW. Input (1)(b) said the two-human-owners rule 'has nothing to attach to yet' because doc 09 models account->APPLICATION and never account->PERSON. EMP_MGRS_ID is the FID's owner, and the SME states that owner RECERTIFIES ANNUALLY — so ownership arrives already as-of, with a stated cadence, which is exactly §B's subject. Raised as Q7. It must NOT be swept into doc 09's contact-column deferral: a recertifying manager is accountability, not a contact point, and input (1)(b) already drew that line. SEPARATE SURFACE, DO NOT CONFLATE: the SME also showed a FID MANAGEMENT TOOL (not the Oracle table) whose record carries a Seal id + seal status, a functional TYPE of Application|Component, support team/email/queue, and OWNER ROLES drawn from the SAME TOM vocabulary as the G35 register (the SEAL* role codes). Two consequences: the FID record and the application TOM register share a role vocabulary, which G70's register seeding should know; and the support team/email/queue columns are precisely §D3's 'OUT for now' set that belongs to email-dl-contact-point. The tool is a THIRD surface beside the table and the export — its columns are not evidence of what HR_PHONE_EXP projects.

Q10Ingest the failure/activity email corpus (.msg + Copilot JSON) with an SME surface for assigning an email to a folder or process
drydocs-docmetaP14requirementp2fable / main
docmeta
depends on: G31

Acceptance: A doc-source-registry entry declares the email corpus with its classification, connector: email, tier, curation ladder, target_db and retention note; the corpus loads as the ACTIVE lexical shape (Document → Chunk) with the source .msg/JSON pair referenced by path, never copied into the repo; and an email whose folder/process is NOT extractable is loadable WITHOUT an assignment, landing unassigned rather than being rejected or guessed. The assignment edge (email Document → ControlMFolder / process) is NEW relationship semantics and goes through the HITL gate: registered `status: planned` in relationship_vocabulary.yaml with a gate-prompt spec, and no loader writes it until the gate confirms. The SME assignment surface itself may be a later slice — this item's floor is "ingested, unassigned, and gate-registered".

Notes: User source 2026-07-26: "we get emails that reference a failure or activity and I've extracted those as json files and save the original msg format... it may require an SME assigning it to a particular folder or process if it's not extractable from the email." RETENTION, and it is the reason the source pair matters: Outlook purges at 6-18 months, but the extracts are deliberately preserved on a file server until the PROCESS OR PROJECT retires — so after ~18 months the file server holds the only copy and becomes a system of record with a backup obligation, not a cache. Purge is therefore project/process-scoped (a property-scoped delete), NOT a database drop — which is why retention did NOT end up being an argument for a separate database, contrary to the initial guess in that session. Same instinct as the "always keep the original requirement" rule. CLASSIFICATION: production-failure email almost certainly Internal- Confidential (real names, real folder names, incident detail). The .msg/JSON originals live OUTSIDE the repo — the gitignored-PDF precedent — and only mechanism-level references are committed. Distinct from the 2026-07-22 email-DL contact-point idea already in IDEAS: that one is about DL membership as an ontology mapping; this is the email BODY as a document corpus. SIBLING CORPUS NOW EXISTS — READ BEFORE BUILDING (2026-08-05, user flagged the relation): `adhoc-sme-email` was registered in config/doc-source-registry.yaml for a one-off SME evidence email, with connector: email and citation-only shape. This item's acceptance says "a doc-source-registry entry declares THE email corpus", singular, so the first decision here is EXTEND vs ADD — not a discovery to make mid-build. Four properties differ (shape: citation-only vs the ACTIVE Document→Chunk spine; cadence: one-off vs recurring feed; retention: only Q10's extracts carry the post-purge backup obligation; assignment: only Q10 needs the email→folder/process edge), which is why they are two entries today. If the SME folds them, the shape difference becomes a per-Document property — cheap now, expensive once either has loaded.

The point that decided this is its own item rather than a rider on the database question: QUARANTINING DOES NOT DISAMBIGUATE. Putting all three versions in an unstructured-content database leaves all three versions sitting together, still ambiguous — the separation protects OTHER corpora from them, it does not tell you which one is current. That is a modeling problem and needs modeling, whatever the topology ends up being. Hence depends_on G31 only for where the nodes live, not for the semantics.

Q15Agent navigation QuerySpecs over the doc spine: name-addressable lookup, section browse, role siblings, search as FALLBACK
drydocs-apiP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta
depends on: Q13

Acceptance: Four registered QuerySpecs — docs.utility-lookup.v1 (exact name -> docs grouped by page_role), docs.section-browse.v1 (section -> siblings, one hop), docs.role-siblings.v1 (doc -> same-subject docs of another role), and docs.search.v1 (full-text/vector, explicitly the FALLBACK for "I don't know the name"). All four: bounded expansion with no unbounded variable-length traversal; every row carries source_url + doc_version + trust so the R5 citation surface renders provenance; chunk text is NOT returned by default — the agent asks for it as a deliberate second step. Proven against the loaded corpus, and reachable from /ask without touching /raw-cypher.

Notes: Section 4 of the plan. The point is that an agent usually arrives already knowing the noun ("how do I use exportdefjob?"), and a vector search for a known exact identifier is both slower and less reliable than an indexed exact match — so similarity search is demoted to the fallback path rather than being the only door in. Chunk-free by default because agent context is the scarce resource: triage on abstract + page_role, spend context on text only after choosing. Specs over raw Cypher per the R4/R5 design (ephemeral specs + citations carrying trust and classification) — this keeps doc answers citable and keeps agents off /raw-cypher.

R7Stale-source detection + rescrape queue: freshness fields on :Document, staleness check at answer time, queued full re-chunk refresh, rescrape-and-re-answer in the Ask spoke
drydocs-docmetaP15requirementp2sonnet / main
agentic-qa
depends on: R5 Q6

Acceptance: :Document nodes carry source_url, source_sha256, fetched_at, refresh policy, and a status lifecycle; answers flag citations whose source is stale per policy; rescrape is a QUEUED refresh artifact — auto-runnable for SYNTHESIZED corpora, re-queues HITL curation for CONFIRMED (the doc-source-registry sha256 rule, now code-enforced, never a silent overwrite); a changed sha triggers FULL re-chunk (a test proves position-resume is not used when content changed); "rescrape & re-answer" round-trips in the Ask spoke with both envelopes kept for comparison.

Notes: CLAIMED THEN RELEASED 2026-08-01 (desktop) — the claim is withdrawn, not abandoned mid-build: nothing was written, so the item is exactly as it was, plus this finding. A pre-build survey found a HARD dependency the item never recorded. "Rescrape is a QUEUED refresh artifact — AUTO-RUNNABLE for SYNTHESIZED corpora" needs something that can actually refetch, and the producer has NO fetcher: the web + filedrop connectors are Q6's deliverable ("Port A: bkup scrapers -> the producer docmeta component"), Q6 is todo and parked on physical media confirmed absent on both machines, and its web connector is additionally gated on Q12's page-count refusal. Building the queue anyway would ship a queue nothing can drain and an "auto-runnable" path that cannot run — worse than not building it, because the surface would claim a capability that does not exist. Q6 therefore added to depends_on. What is NOT blocked, and why a SPLIT is the obvious alternative for the user to rule rather than for an agent to assume: clauses (a) the :Document freshness fields + status lifecycle, (b) staleness flagging on citations, and (d) full re-chunk on a changed sha are all buildable today against the existing loaders — only the auto-run rescrape and the Ask spoke's round-trip need the fetcher. Splitting freshness-now from rescrape-later would unblock roughly three quarters of this item. One further gap the survey turned up, cheap to fix inside whichever shape wins: `agents/graph_qa/pipeline.py` hardcodes `"chunks": 0` in two places with the comment "doc-chunk retrieval arrives with R7 corpora wiring", so the agent currently has no Document-sourced SourceRecord at all. Clause (b) is still reachable without new retrieval architecture — the O18 docs QuerySpecs already return doc_ids, so a routed docs spec's rows can be joined to Document freshness and stamped onto the existing SourceRecord.fetched_at/stale slots — but the item's inputs name neither the pipeline nor the specs, so whoever builds it should widen them.

S12Environment-drift guard: the suite fails loudly when the interpreter's packages disagree with poetry.lock
drydocs-coreP6chorep2sonnet / main
structure-remediation

Acceptance: A session-scoped guard in tests/conftest.py reads poetry.lock, and for every locked package that is ALSO installed in the running interpreter, asserts the installed version equals the locked one. Packages absent from the interpreter are skipped, not failed — the lock carries groups and extras a given install legitimately does not select. On drift the guard fails the session ONCE, before any test runs, naming sys.prefix, the count, and the first few offenders as `name locked X, installed Y`; it must also name the usual cause (an inherited VIRTUAL_ENV taking precedence over the in-project venv) and the remedy, because the failure the guard replaces was misread as twenty broken tests. Guard on DRIFT, never on the venv PATH: a path assertion would fail Docker, tox and system-python runs that are correctly provisioned, and would miss a wrong-version install inside the right directory. Proven both ways, and the fixture for the negative case is already on this machine: DryDocs/.venv reports zero drift across 65 installed locked packages and the suite stays green, while the shared sandbox venv reports 16 — including click (locked 8.1.8, installed 8.3.2) and ruff (locked 0.5.7, installed 0.15.11). A unit test drives the comparison function over synthetic lock/installed pairs so the negative case is reproducible off this machine. CI green on both matrix versions — CI installs from the lock, so it has no drift by construction.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-18, the follow-up the S11 session's venv note (internal/repo-README.md, PR #3) deliberately left out. The note tells a reader what to do; nothing MAKES the wrong environment announce itself. What it costs today: poetry honours an already-activated VIRTUAL_ENV ahead of the in-project venv poetry.toml pins, so a shell with another environment active runs the suite against that one. Under click >= 8.3 typer 0.12's secondary flags raise TypeError and about twenty CLI tests go red — tests that are not broken. That cost a full investigation cycle during the S11 work, and it is self-concealing: the suite looks broken, CI looks green, and the two disagree for a reason nothing on screen explains. The click case is the CHEAP one. The same venv carries ruff 0.15.11 against the exact 0.5.7 pin that pyproject calls load-bearing (J10 stage 0, authority docs/ruff-format-convergence.md) because formatter output varies across versions. A `ruff format` run from the wrong environment reformats the tree to a different convention and lands a diff CI then blocks — the failure J10 exists to prevent, and the one that ran RED for 100+ consecutive runs between 2026-08-05 and 08-12 without anyone looking. That is the real argument for p2 rather than the p3 its S8/S9 siblings carry: this guard protects a gate that has already failed silently once. Placement is tests/conftest.py, not tests/unit/ — integration runs deserve the same guard, and the file already owns session-scoped concerns (the shared Neo4j driver teardown). REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: assert sys.prefix equals the repo .venv. Simpler to write and wrong — it fails correctly-provisioned runs that are not in-project, and passes a mismatched install that happens to sit in the right folder. Drift is the defect; the path is only its most common cause, and belongs in the failure MESSAGE rather than the assertion. SEPARATE, do not fold in: `poetry run pytest` needs PYTHONPATH=. locally or tests/unit/conftest.py cannot import drydocs_core, while `poetry run python -c "import drydocs_core"` succeeds. CI does not hit it. Different defect, own item.

Notes: Raised at the business-application-identity gate §F2 (SIGNED OFF 2026-07-27). SME reason, verbatim in substance: the glossary will for the most part be internal unless there are industry-standard acronyms or names, and doing the scaffolding producer-side now means the internal ports do not collide later with either a name or a backlog item. That is a PORT-SEQUENCING argument, not an ontology one — which is why reservation is the whole deliverable. WHY IT IS AN ITEM RATHER THAN AN ACT OF THAT GATE: the identity gate's §A1 states it "creates no relationship-vocabulary term". Registering the edges inside it would have falsified A1 and re-opened a ruled scope item, so the registration was pushed here, where `status: planned` needs no gate of its own. Substance this feeds: F2's finding that the durable home for what an acronym MEANS is a CatalogBusinessTerm-shaped glossary, the same conclusion the reopened gate-log Q6 acronym question circles, plus the Unity Catalog takeaway that a controlled vocabulary needs an enforcement point or it rots. The identity gate is itself the evidence: "SEAL" was found carrying THREE distinct meanings across three homes (the issuing authority, the source id, and an ecosystem referencing convention used in Control-M CMDLINEs), and nothing in the repo recorded that they were different things. MERGED IN 2026-08-05 (desktop, Idea-35 — the acronym-catalog line): that entry is CONTENT for this scaffold, not a second home, and it names the shape the scaffold should be able to hold — which is worth knowing while building the empty version. Its requirement: key by acronym, carry MANY senses per key, and tag each sense with its scope (`area`, `business-domain`, `technical-domain`, `industry` — what an outsider would assume). Plus, wherever a misreading has actually happened, an explicit **does-NOT-mean** note; that note, not the expansion, is the protective sentence. AIS is the worked example and the reason: "as-is" (a standard modeling idiom) vs "Application Integration Streaming" (an org platform family), with our own `:AisTool` label having meant NEITHER. Today `software-registry.yaml#acronyms` is a one-key section with no scope dimension, so it can record expansions but not COLLISIONS — and collisions are the failure mode that bites. This is a SKOS job (prefLabel / altLabel / definition / scopeNote, senses as concepts in a scheme); SKOS is declared in reference/standards/README.md but has NO fetched local copy yet, unlike prov-o / w3c-org / dprod-ekgf / sosa-ssn — fetching it belongs with the content pass. SCAFFOLD-ONLY STILL HOLDS: this item defines no terms, so nothing above changes its acceptance. The content pass stays parked on its own trigger, the gate-log Q6 ruling (which decides whether `#acronyms` survives at all), and lands INSIDE this scaffold.

(2) config/taxonomy/business-application.yaml's `roles:` list is DELETED, not reinterpreted — §F3 named leaving both as the one outcome to refuse. Note `roles:` is DERIVED from the memberships block, so the membership blocks move with it. (3) THE REGISTER IS SEEDED FROM THE SIGNED §G: REQUIRED = application_owner, primary_information_owner, backup_information_owner, cto, technology_risk_controls, design_authority, backup_application_owner. AND READ THE REGISTER MARKER RATHER THAN RECONSTRUCTING IT: the catalog's own description text labels the SEAL-sourced rows ('... from SEAL'), which IS the two-register mapping §A asked for. Read it and verify; do not derive it. Note `type` is weakly populated (mostly 'other'), so it is not a reliable classifier on its own, and most of the 83 rows are out of scope — MARK those rather than dropping them, so the file's coverage stays legible. SRE IS A SPECIAL CASE — AMENDED 2026-08-11 after the sign-off, see the gate-log amendment. It is OPTIONAL *and DERIVED*: an SRE team serves 1:many applications (roughly 20-60), so it is a shared function pointing at many apps rather than a per-application holding, and its presence is READ FROM THE GROUP NAMING CONVENTION's function segment rather than asserted. Seed it with a `derived: true` marker so G71's completeness report can EXCLUDE it — a derived many-to-one fact in a per-application required-contact report generates a finding on every application whose SRE team simply was not asserted. AND DO NOT PATTERN-MATCH THE ROLE NAME: in the sampled data an SRE-named role resolves to a SUPPORT-function group (the team reuses one), so the role label disagrees with the group and the GROUP is right. (5) RISK MANAGER CROSSWALKS TO technology_risk_controls (§A2 ruled: one class, two names) — and STOPS THERE. The SEAL-risk ↔ ServiceNow-group mapping is NOT known and no group resolution is designed for it (signed residual 1). (6) SealRole IS RETIRED AS THE ADMISSION GATE (§A3/§F4): an unrecognised name LOADS flagged undeclared instead of raising ValidationError and killing the row. _ROLE_CANONICAL survives as an alias table. The four classes today's code rejects outright must load after this. (7) EVERY DOWNSTREAM SURFACE AMENDED IN THE SAME UNIT: the supplement's scheme seed, both loader crosswalks, the map entry's role_vocabulary text, the vocabulary fragment, NODE_QUICK_REFERENCE.md, and the seal-extract field ledger's "kept verbatim" claim (§A4b — the raw source string must survive ALONGSIDE the canonical one, not instead of it). Either carry a migration step or rebuild from source — say which. The attribution_id 4-part shape itself is UNTOUCHED (identity gate §D2). Suite green; no graph write beyond the supplement re-run.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 at the G35 sign-off. THE ONE-UNIT RULE IS THE POINT — §A8 showed the vocabulary living in four hardcoded places, and §A1b showed the one YAML copy drifting twice inside a single gate with the full suite passing both times, because no code reads it. G35 §A ruled BOTH REGISTERS, so this file is not a list of 13 names: it holds the ServiceNow catalog's 100+ types with their Scope and Type, the SEAL extract's names, and the mapping. Only ~28 types were observed instantiated on one sampled application, so the file should distinguish DECLARED from OBSERVED rather than implying every catalog entry is in use. THE DENOMINATOR IS RULED (§C6): only applications a feed actually covered. G73Inheritance: assertion mode + a modelled ancestor edge, authored rows only — and the ancestor-CI widening that K21 §7.4 needs
ontologyP9taskp2fable / main
seal-attribution
depends on: G70

Acceptance: Per the signed §E. THE LOAD STORES AUTHORED ROWS ONLY: of the three Inheritance states, Direct (blank) and Overridden are AUTHORED; Inherited rows are DERIVED COPIES carrying two lineage pointers. Inheritance is computed, not materialised — storing a derived fact as though asserted is how a graph starts disagreeing with its source. THE ANCESTOR IS A MODELLED EDGE, not a property (§E4 ruled), so "why does this application show a different owner than its parent" is TRAVERSABLE — which is what §D2 says an operator cannot do today. Both lineage references are load-bearing: the ancestor CI and the ancestor ROW. IT IS ONE MECHANISM UP AN N-LEVEL CHAIN, not a two-level relation (§E1e): "copy from the nearest ancestor holding the role", applied repeatedly. A model built for a fixed application→deployment relation cannot represent the observed pass-through case, where a role originates two rungs up and passes straight through the application untouched. OVERRIDES PROPAGATE: a child inherits the ancestor's CURRENT value even when that value is itself an Override, so the effective holder can differ from the top of the chain. AND IT AMENDS THE PULL SCOPE — this is the item that carries it. Reconstructing an inherited holder requires ANCESTOR CIs, which sit ABOVE the ~200 applications DryDocs supports, including CIs owned by teams it does not. K21 §7.4 is amended to take ancestor CIs FOR THEIR TOM ROWS ONLY, and the amendment is written there rather than left implicit.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 at the G35 sign-off. This is the first place the ~200-application boundary and the inheritance model actually conflict, and the gate crossed it deliberately rather than quietly. The alternative — materialise inherited rows and flag them derived — stays inside the boundary and was considered and rejected: it duplicates, and it drifts when an ancestor changes.

Acceptance: TWO CLAUSES, one spine. Per the signed §B7. The TOM load links an Attribution to a PERSON and stops; placing that person in the reporting structure is separate work on a separate cadence. THE DEFERRAL CURRENTLY POINTS AT NOTHING, which is what this item fixes: :Employee is a node class with NO Employee-to-Employee edge anywhere in the relationship vocabulary — no REPORTS_TO, no manager edge — and until this item there was no backlog entry that would create one. Scope: propose the edge and its provenance, route it through docs/RELATIONSHIP_GUIDE.md and the relationship-vocabulary registry as status: planned, and identify the SOURCE that could populate it. DO NOT BUILD A LOADER — the source question is the real one, and the producer-side HR hierarchy direction (two-scope HR supplement, two-pass loader, REPORTS_TO current-state sweep) is company-gated work that this item must not pre-empt. A CLOSER SOURCE MAY EXIST: group-scoped TOM roles resolve to sys_user_group MEMBERS today, which is a people-graph of a different shape — adjacency rather than hierarchy. Say whether that is a route or a distraction. SECOND CLAUSE, ADDED 2026-08-11 (SME, from a desktop session) — RULE THE :Employee CREATION POLICY, BECAUSE THE DOC AND THE CODE CONTRADICT EACH OTHER AND BOTH ARE DEFENSIBLE. The runbook's "spine-and-enrich" rule, in BOTH v2 and the published v3, states that :Employee is created ONLY by load-employee-roster and that SEAL attaches enrich-only via OPTIONAL MATCH — "a SID not in the roster gets no edge, never a stub". seal_applications.cypher does the OPPOSITE: it MERGEs (e:Employee {employee_id: <owner/CTO/info-owner SID>}) ON CREATE SET e.source = 'SEAL', minting placeholders. DIRECTION LANDED 2026-08-18 (SME in-chat, gate-log RECORD same date): STUB-AND-ENRICH WINS. "The HR database has ~300k; my expectation is that it will be the stub and supplemented with HR data later." The loader behavior is the policy; the runbook text is what must change. What this item still owes: harmonize the runbook (v2 + published v3), rule the stub property idiom (what marks awaiting-enrichment beyond `source`), and clause 1 (REPORTS_TO + its source) in full. pat_team_roles.cypher was flipped to the MERGE-stub idiom in the RECORD's commit. MEASURED STATE (desktop graph, 2026-08-11): 11,464 :Employee nodes, ALL source='SEAL', every one minted by the seal_applications load. They carry employee_id + full_name and NO REPORTS_TO — there is no HR spine yet. 11,445 are HAS_AGENT targets of ownership attributions; 19 are unattached (likely CTO/info-owner SIDs whose attribution did not land, or delete leftovers). THE MECHANISM IS SOUND AND SELF-RECONCILING, which is why this is a ruling and not a bug: load-employee-roster MERGEs on the SAME key and unconditionally flips source SEAL -> HR (authoritative), so a SID in both is upgraded and gains the REPORTS_TO spine, a roster-only SID is created fresh as HR, and a SID in SEAL but in no loaded HR subtree STAYS source='SEAL'. That residual is a COVERAGE REPORT, not debris — count the source='SEAL' survivors after a roster load and you have the owners HR did not cover. The placeholders are intentional and keyed to reconcile. RULE ONE OF TWO, and record which: (a) FIX THE DOC to describe the placeholder pattern, keeping the code's behaviour — it preserves the ownership SID and name that would otherwise be LOST whenever the roster is not loaded, and the source flag keeps them cleanly reconcilable; or (b) FIX THE LOADER to OPTIONAL MATCH, if roster-only really is the intent — at the cost of dropping ownership identity when the roster is absent. NOT A MID-LOAD DECISION and not urgent: the graph is safe to run load-employee-roster against as it stands. What is NOT acceptable is leaving a design doc that forbids what the loader does, since the next reader trusts whichever they happen to open. THE RULING HAS A COMPANY-SIDE HALF, VERIFIED PRODUCER-SIDE 2026-08-11 — DO NOT RULE IT HERE ALONE. Only ONE of the three surfaces is producer-side: drydocs/loaders/cypher/seal_applications.cypher DOES mint the placeholders, at lines 145 / 169 / 192, for app_owner_sid, chief_tech_officer_sid and info_owner_sid respectively — checkable from here. The OTHER TWO ARE NOT. There is no employee-roster loader producer-side (no load-employee-roster verb, no roster cypher; the port-prompt already records tests/unit/test_employee_roster.py as company-only, T21), and the "spine-and-enrich" runbook prose that FORBIDS the stub appears in no producer runbook under docs/design/. So the producer holds the code that mints, and the company holds both the doc that forbids it AND the loader that reconciles it. CONSEQUENCE: the producer can rule what ITS loader should do, but it cannot fix a doc it does not have, and it cannot verify the reconciliation half. Route this ruling through the port rather than landing it one-sided — the same asymmetry class as RELAY-6, and it is the second time this session that a producer-side item turned out to overlap company-only material.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 at the G35 sign-off, on the SME's instruction that the deferral needed an owner. THE SECOND CLAUSE ARRIVED THE SAME DAY and belongs here rather than in its own item because it is the SAME SPINE: clause one asks what creates the Employee-to-Employee edge, clause two asks what is allowed to create the :Employee NODE. Ruling the second without the first would settle the node policy while leaving the hierarchy homeless, and ruling the first without the second would build a spine on top of an unruled creation policy. It is this item's clause one asked from the other end, so it rides here rather than opening a second owner. O44Ownership reconciliation ALLUVIAL diagram (a Sankey variant): four ordered columns — employee hierarchy | SEAL/TOM contacts | ServiceNow queues + technicians | PAT structure — with ribbons where an entity appears in both, and a terminating ribbon where it does not
drydocs-webP12requirementp2sonnet / main
web-console
depends on: G35

Acceptance: THE DIAGRAM TYPE IS NAMED, and it is not decoration: this is an ALLUVIAL diagram — the Sankey family variant for CATEGORICAL data across several ordered dimensions, where the same entities are re-partitioned column by column and ribbons carry membership from one partition to the next. (SME 2026-08-05, correcting this item's first draft, which described the shape and never named it.) Sankey is the family; alluvial is the member, and the distinction decides the data contract — a general Sankey moves a QUANTITY between distinct nodes, an alluvial moves the SAME ENTITIES between categorizations. Build to the alluvial contract: nodes = (column, category), links = (source category, target category, the entity set that is in both). A console pane rendering FOUR ordered columns over the same applications and people, each column a different system's view of who owns what, with a ribbon drawn ONLY where the entity is actually present in both adjacent columns' lists (the SME framing). THE TERMINATING RIBBON IS THE PRODUCT. An entity that appears in one column and not the next does not fade out quietly — a flow that stops IS the finding, and it must be visually distinct from a flow that continues. That is what makes this the reconciliation surface for G35 §D: a SEAL contact with no ServiceNow counterpart is a roster disagreement made legible, and a diagram that only draws matches would hide precisely the case it exists for. (1) EMPLOYEE HIERARCHY, filterable by manager. (2) SEAL/TOM CONTACTS, filterable by SEAL id, LOB, product line, product and contact role. (3) SERVICENOW: the queues/assignment groups matching the applications in column 1's list, showing their technician roles. (4) PAT STRUCTURE with its SEALs. SHIP IN PHASES, and the phase boundary is a DATA boundary, not a UI one — columns 2 and 4 are buildable today, columns 1 and 3 are not (see notes). Phase 1 acceptance is columns 2+4 with the cross-column relationship drawn and the two missing columns shown as EXPLICITLY EMPTY WITH A REASON, never omitted: a four-column pane silently rendering two columns is the failure this acceptance exists to prevent. Every column names its source system and the freshness of its load. Full suite green.

Notes: SME direction 2026-08-05, in-chat during the G35 gate draft. This is the surface where G35 §D's roster disagreement becomes VISIBLE rather than inferred — §D3 proposes recording which surface an attribution came from, and this pane is what consumes it, which is why it depends_on G35 rather than merely citing it. DATA STATE, measured 2026-08-05 (this is the whole reason it ships in phases): * COLUMN 2 (SEAL/TOM) — EXISTS. Attribution/TOMRole/Employee load today, and every requested filter is backed by a real node: CatalogLOB, ProductLine, Product, BusinessApplication, and the contact role itself. The K11 steward cascade already implements Product Line -> Product -> Business Application, so the filter chain is a reuse, not a build. * COLUMN 4 (PAT) — EXISTS. Product/AreaProduct/DevTeam load via pat_product_mapping.cypher + area_products.cypher, and pat:people-report carries team-scoped seal_ids. Caveat recorded at C17: the people report projects Sponsoring Product Line as a NAME ONLY, so that grain stays unmodelled and the column cannot filter on it. * COLUMN 1 (EMPLOYEE HIERARCHY) — DOES NOT EXIST. :Employee is a node class (prov:Agent) with NO Employee-to-Employee edge anywhere in the relationship vocabulary: no REPORTS_TO, no manager edge, no source feeding one, and no backlog item that would create one. The manager filter is the column's whole point and there is nothing to filter on. G35 §B7 defers hierarchy placement to "a later pass" on SME direction; this item is the first consumer that makes the missing owner concrete. * COLUMN 3 (SERVICENOW) — NOT INGESTED. snow:cmdb-ci-classes is registered (Q4 ruling, 2026-07-31) but confirmed: false, adapter: ~, and it is a header-only capture of CMDB CLASSES — not queues, not assignment groups, not people. The "SEAL technician roles" the SME describes appear in the repo only as prose: the runbook skill's template-spec cites AO/RE Snow queues with a Technician role, and internal/remediation names a SNOW technician group + CTASK. That is enough to know the concept is real and not enough to build a column. RIBBON WEIGHT IS AN OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, flagged rather than assumed: in a Sankey the ribbon THICKNESS encodes a quantity, and this diagram has more than one candidate — count of people, count of applications, or unweighted equal-width membership bands. Pick before building; retrofitting a weight changes the layout engine's input, not just a style. NO LIBRARY IN THE STACK DOES THIS. web/package.json carries @xyflow/react (node-and-edge graphs, not flows) and d3-force (force layout). An alluvial needs d3-sankey or a hand-rolled SVG with a crossing-minimisation pass — readable column ordering is most of the work in this diagram, and it is the part a naive implementation gets wrong. A new dependency also lands in the software registry, which is the third-party ledger, so it is a registration as well as an install. NOT SPLIT INTO SEPARATE ITEMS on purpose: the two missing columns are SOURCE questions (does DryDocs ingest the HR hierarchy and the SNOW queue export, producer-side or company-side?) and that is a user decision, not an agent's. Both are inboxed against this item rather than groomed into speculative work. If the answer is company-side for either, this item's phase 1 IS its final scope and the acceptance says so.

Acceptance: Per-SME quality signals derive from intake records the store already holds — no new data entry: submissions in a rolling window, auto-accept rate (agent candidates accepted with zero modification), too-fast rate (confirm faster than a floor scaled to evidence size), and admin-return rate. G56Collector captures the mount table, so shared-vs-local storage is DERIVED instead of declared (bundle schema v3)
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A bundle answers "is this path on shared storage?" without asking a human. The collector emits an OPTIONAL mounts section capturing actual mount state — `findmnt -rn -o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS` with `/proc/mounts` as the no-findmnt fallback, both read-only and runnable as the service account with no privilege change. NOT lsblk and NOT /etc/fstab alone, and the script says why in a comment: `server:/path` is an NFS mount spec and NFS is not a block device, so it never appears in lsblk; and fstab is configured INTENT, not actual state (autofs/systemd/manual mounts are mounted without appearing there, stale lines appear without being mounted). COLLECTOR_VERSION bumps to v3. The extractor parses the section when present and files it under the EXISTING `sections_optional_absent` contract when absent, so every v1 and v2 bundle stays fully ingestible — the same discipline scripts.tsv already follows. Each staged path resolves against the LONGEST matching mount target to yield `mount_root` + `fstype`, and `storage_scope` derives from fstype — nfs/nfs4/cifs shared, xfs/ext4 single-host unless gfs2/ocfs2 clustered, anything unrecognised `unknown` and COUNTED, never guessed. Synthetic fixtures only (real mount specs carry live server names); tests cover a shared-NFS bundle, a local-only bundle, a mounts-absent v2 bundle, and an unrecognised fstype.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-06 (laptop) at the G22 session, from SME direction. THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES: a deployment path may be shared — the SME's case is roughly 20 VSI hosts against one shared filesystem — and then the same path on N hosts is ONE FILE SEEN N TIMES, not N deployments. Today that is not derivable from any bundle we hold: the collector captures no mount table at all, the envelope carries scan_roots but never which filesystem a root sits on, and the ownership sweep's -xdev stays on one filesystem without recording which. THE CORRECTION THAT SHAPES THE ACCEPTANCE, made at the session: "on the SAN" does not mean shared. Twenty hosts each with their OWN LUN from one array is twenty separate filesystems and twenty files that genuinely drift; twenty hosts mounting ONE NFS export is one file seen twenty times. Sharing follows from FSTYPE, never from the array — which is why the type column is load-bearing and why lsblk alone would actively mislead. WHY NOW IS THE CHEAP MOMENT (SME, same session): nothing has been loaded yet and the company-side twin collector is NOT present, so a schema bump costs no convergence debt. The earlier T14 caveat is WITHDRAWN on that correction. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REMOVE: bundles already collected stay scope-unknown, so the G22 D-amendment rule stands either way — `unknown` never defaults to independent, it SUPPRESSES the corroboration claim. This item reduces how often that state occurs; it does not retire it. NOT gate-bound: capturing a fact is an instrument change, not a decision about what an edge MEANS. It was deliberately NOT edited at the gate because the collector runs on production hosts.

G68Folder-set PROFILE over a staged Control-M XML export: the FID/variable/email census plus the substitution slots the XML cannot answer
drydocs-remediationP6taskp1opus / main
component-topology
depends on: G67

Acceptance: A `profile()` over a DefinitionSet (so it runs on anything xml_bridge already stages -- NO new parser) returning ONE JSON-serializable FolderSetProfile that answers "what is in this folder set" for a reader who already knows the process. Four censuses, each carrying WHERE-USED rather than bare distinct values, because the SME's next question is always which jobs: (a) SHAPE -- folders, sub-folders, job counts by type (file watcher / placement / trust / other), and the datasets inferred from the sub-folder ladder; (b) IDENTITY -- distinct FID, RUN_AS, SEAL and application values with the jobs carrying each; (c) VARIABLES -- every declared name by scope with its distinct-value count, reference count, and its R30/R31 state inline, so the census and the defect list are one table and not two the reader has to join by hand; (d) CONTACTS -- every EMAIL_DL_* value and every DOMAIL destination found, split by contact kind (support tier vs Production Delay Notification consumer) and labelled documentation-only, since R40 now deletes the block that would have used them. Then the half the census cannot produce: a SUBSTITUTION SLOT list -- the facts the XML does not carry and only the SME can supply (DEVX_KEY, the MFTS set FTS_ID / REC_ID / USER / DELIVERY_MECHANISM, EMAIL_DL_L2 / L3 / PDN, SOURCE_CONTACT). Each slot names its current value or records it ABSENT, its vocabulary or shape rule from the guidelines page, and the jobs it would apply to. A slot with no current value is "not supplied", NEVER a default: inventing one is how a proposal becomes a wrong fact nobody re-checks. The profile ASSERTS NOTHING about meaning -- it is a census, findings stay detect_all()'s output and ride alongside, and nothing here ratifies or writes a graph (the module's standing invariant). Committed fixtures are synthetic, since real FIDs, SEALs and DLs are Internal. The TRANSPORT is named in the item's commit rather than defaulted, per the O58 precedent: a CLI verb writing a JSON artifact is the recommended first pass, because remediation writes no graph (so QuerySpecs are out by construction) and no upload path exists yet -- but if an API endpoint is chosen instead, the commit body records the choice and its cost against ADR 0005.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 on SME direction, as the read half of the remediation loop the SME calls the bulk of the project's intent: read the Control-M estate (database primary, XML secondary), map the flow, and the first pass is already enough to generate the Excel runbook -- .claude/skills/controlm-runbook-automation-excel consumes the same facts, so this profile is a feed for it and not a parallel one. WHY A PROFILE AND NOT A REPORT: the SME is assumed to KNOW the process. What they cannot see is what the XML actually says -- which FIDs are in play, which variable names really exist and at what scope, which contacts are carried. Show them that, and they can supply the DEVX_KEY, the MFTS routes and the contacts that get substituted in. That division -- machine reports what IS, SME supplies what is NOT THERE -- is what keeps this out of the guessing that produced the drift C30 documents. Deliberately NOT in scope: emitting corrected XML. XmlDefinitionFormat.dump() still raises pending the vendor schema, and the profile plus the SME's substitutions are a PROPOSAL, which is what the equivalence proof already consumes.

G69R41-R44: the four fan-out defect classes get their registry entries and their detectors in the SAME change, so neither can exist without the other
drydocs-remediationP6taskp2opus / main
component-topology
depends on: C32

Acceptance: Four defect classes C32 observed with no rule to hold them are registered AND detected in one change. The pairing is the item: the registry is the single source for both the validate gate and the greenfield gate, so a detector with no entry emits findings nothing can rank, nothing can turn into a fix, and -- the real problem -- nothing can SIGN OFF on. The entry is the thing that gets ratified. (a) R41 DUPLICATE DECLARATION IN ONE SCOPE -- one name declared twice in the same container with different values. Live: RPATH twice in one folder, a relative path and an absolute one. Severity must-fix, not should-fix: which value wins is an ordinal accident, so the job runs against whichever declaration happens to be last, and the reader of the folder sees both and cannot tell. (b) R42 FOLDER-NAME DELIMITER DRIFT -- one folder set mixing separators between the same positional fields, so a SQL parse splitting on the delimiter returns different field counts per folder. Live: two folders of one set using an underscore where their siblings use a hyphen. This is the rule whose finding must name the PARSE consequence, not the cosmetic one. (c) R43 CARRIER COLLISION -- one name resolved by two different resolvers in one command line: a Control-M %%VAR beside a shell ${VAR}. THE ENTRY MUST RULE WHICH CARRIER OWNS THE NAME BEFORE THE DETECTOR SHIPS, because the greenfield action differs completely by answer -- rename one carrier, or declare the shell export -- and a detector that fires without that ruling produces findings no one can act on. If the ruling is not available, R43 is registered status OPEN with no detector and the item says so; it does NOT ship a detector against an undecided rule. (d) R44 STALE AUTHORED PROVENANCE -- an authored "created by" field that travelled with a copied job, so it names the template's author rather than the job's. Detectable as one value across jobs whose independent audit trail names different users. Advisory severity, and the finding must say what to read INSTEAD (the creation/modification audit fields), since the value is not wrong so much as answering a different question. All four land status PROVISIONAL and emit ratified=False, per the module rule that only ratified rules may change a definition. Each gets its entry in the existing registry shape (check / engine / severity / status / source / greenfield action), a detector in the conformance pass, and a case in the drifted fixture -- with the greenfield fixture still raising ZERO findings, which is the assertion that the standard stays reachable. Suite green, ruff clean, publish-boundary clean.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) at SME request, immediately after C32 listed the four classes and deliberately did not build them. THE REASON THIS IS ITS OWN ITEM RATHER THAN A WIDENING OF G67: G67 shipped R30-R40 as a closed set with a signed-off shape. Adding rules to it means either reopening a done item or quietly growing it, and the second is exactly how a rule set stops matching the registry that is supposed to govern it -- the failure the pairing rule exists to prevent, committed by the change that implements the pairing rule. SCOPE DISCIPLINE, stated because three of these are easy and one is not: R41, R42 and R44 are mechanical and would ratify quickly. R43 is a genuine question about which carrier owns a name, and its answer changes what a fix even looks like. Do not let the three easy ones carry the hard one over the line -- shipping R43 as provisional-with-detector when the ownership question is open would put a finding in front of an SME that has no defensible action attached to it. NOT IN SCOPE: ratifying any of them. That is the HITL gate's, and it wants real findings from a real folder set rather than fixture hits -- which is what G68's profile run produces. The governance walk-through these four are the worked example of lives in drydocs_remediation/overview_readme.md.

Acceptance: Two gaps in the same manifest vocabulary, closed together because both are "the disposition set is missing a value" on one file with one reviewer. G81DATA LOSS: every path the system reads or writes must be DECLARED in configuration with a mode, and no write path may contain a read path
drydocs-coreP6bugp0opus / main
component-topology

Acceptance: INCIDENT, 2026-08-11: the SME's internal folder holding extracted CSV source data was OVERWRITTEN. Recovery is from a backup, so the data is not lost, but the class is live and it fires again the moment the backup is restored to the same place. This is the most severe defect class the repo has produced — every other failure this week was a wrong READ; this one destroyed a source. (a) RECONSTRUCT FIRST, do not guess. Establish what wrote over what, from the code, and record it. The write-capable surface to walk: drydocs_core/data_root.py declares ten-plus path helpers IN PYTHON, several taking create=True so they mkdir, and rua_extracted_dir() names an "extracted" area that a re-run may legitimately rebuild. Reconstruction is part of the deliverable, not a preamble to it — a guard written against a guessed mechanism guards the wrong thing. (b) DECLARE EVERY PATH IN CONFIGURATION, not in code, each carrying a MODE: read (source data the system may NEVER write), write (outputs it owns and may rebuild), scratch (disposable). Three families the SME named, all currently scattered: LOGS (DRYDOCS_LOGDIR, env-only), LOADER INPUT DATA (per source), and REMEDIATION OUTPUT (the greenfield artifact and Jira handoff). Moving the declaration out of Python is the point: today a path is whatever a helper returns, so no reader can enumerate what the system touches, which is why an overlap was invisible until it destroyed something. (c) THE INVARIANT THAT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED IT: no write-mode path may EQUAL OR CONTAIN a read-mode path. Guarded, with the failure naming both paths. This is the whole defect in one sentence and it is mechanically checkable. (d) NO SILENT DEFAULT ROOT. resolve_data_root() falls back to ~/data/DryDocs whenever DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is unset or empty, so a missing environment variable silently relocates every read and write to a plausible-looking wrong place — the SAME defect family as G78's fixture-directory default, one layer down. An unset root must FAIL, naming the variable. (e) Any path a create=True helper may build is write-mode BY CONSTRUCTION. A read-mode path must be reachable through a helper that cannot create, cannot clean and cannot write. Ties to ADR 0012: a source declaring acquisition file-drop needs a declared location, and that location is read-mode by definition — so (b) supplies what the ADR's acquisition axis assumes exists.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) from an SME incident report. p0 on IRREVERSIBILITY, which is the axis that separates it from G78: a wrong load is re-runnable, a destroyed source directory is recoverable only as far as the last backup, and if that backup had been stale or absent the loss would be permanent. G78 is louder; this one is worse. SME DIRECTION ON SEQUENCING: the layout must be planned with the ARCHITECT PERSONA, and it must be planned WITH the loader restructure rather than after it — G79 moves loaders between chains and ADR 0012 puts acquisition on the source entry, so both touch exactly the paths this item declares. Doing the declaration afterwards means declaring a layout that was just rearranged. The persona review is docs/reviews/persona-python-architect — a layout question, not a graph-modelling one, so the Python architect rather than the Neo4j architect. SCOPE FENCE: this declares paths and guards the overlap. It does not relocate anyone's data — a config change that silently moved a root would be the same class of defect the item exists to close.

G78A load step that cannot find its input MUST FAIL — today it silently skips, and a default run loads synthetic fixtures while reporting success
drydocs-loadP6bugp0opus / main
component-topology

Acceptance: TWO DEFECTS, one failure. (1) A chain step whose expected input file is absent logs "No sample for ..., skipping" and the run reports SUCCESS. (2) refresh-reference's only input option is --samples-dir, which DEFAULTS to the bundled fixture directory, so a run with no arguments loads synthetic rows into a real graph and calls it done. Together they produce the worst outcome available: not a failed load, a load that SUCCEEDED with the wrong data -- the confidently-wrong-row class promoted to the load. REPRODUCED ON BOTH SIDES, not theorised. Producer: REFRESH_REFERENCE_CHAIN expects seal_application_data__sample.csv and seal_contact_data__sample.csv and NEITHER EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO (find returns nothing), so the SEAL half of the reference load has never run on bundled fixtures and nothing has ever said so. Company-side: the same skip dropped dev_teams, and a real-data run silently loaded fixtures instead (SME session 2026-08-11). FIX, in three parts: (a) A missing REQUIRED input FAILS the step, naming the file and the path searched. A step may declare an input optional; optional then means written down, not inferred from a file's absence. (b) Real runs stop defaulting to the fixture directory. Production data must not have to be named *_sample.csv in a directory called samples to be loadable -- that is a semantic contradiction the operator is currently forced into. Implement the interface the TDDs ALREADY DESCRIBE and neither side built: --source <source-id> resolving its location from config/source-registry.yaml, with --samples-dir retained for fixtures only. THE CORRECT BEHAVIOUR IS ALREADY IN THE REPO, ONE VERB AWAY, and this clause is closer to making two commands agree than to designing an interface (SME-confirmed 2026-08-11: "--csv works fine changing to a different path"). `drydocs load <name> --csv <path>` takes an ARBITRARY path -- no directory convention, no filename convention, no fixture default -- and when neither --csv nor --sql is given it PRINTS AND EXITS 2 rather than guessing. It also runs the confirmed-gate before any write. So the defect is not "loaders cannot take a path"; it is that the SEQUENCED chain verb behaves worse than the manual verb beside it. Copy the single-loader contract up into the chain: explicit path or fail, never a plausible default. Do NOT rebuild what `load` already does correctly. (c) The run summary states, per step, WHICH path it read and how many rows it loaded, so "it succeeded" is falsifiable at a glance. (d) COVERAGE RIDER, merged from Idea-119 at the 2026-08-13 groom and scoped to this item's own blast radius: the loaders whose step contract this change touches gain a DIRECT test import. FIVE have none today -- drydocs/loaders/business_segments.py, controlm.py, controlm_dependencies_derived.py, controlm_hosts.py and seal_contacts.py (A5 measured 2026-08-13 at bb9788b6: 31 package modules with no direct test import, of which these five are loaders). A test that imports the loader and exercises the missing-input path satisfies this clause and the guard below at once. NOT a general coverage sweep: five named files, because the tests belong with the fix that touches them. Guard: a test proves a chain step with a missing required input FAILS BY NAME, and that a run against the fixture directory is distinguishable in the summary from a run against a declared source.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) from a company-side diagnosis the SME relayed, then reproduced producer-side. p0 because it is silent, it is live on both machines, and every downstream claim about what the graph contains rests on it. Independent of the naming epic -- this is correctness, that is generalization; do not couple them. THERE IS A WORKING ESCAPE HATCH TODAY, and an operator blocked on this should be told rather than left waiting for the fix: `drydocs load <name> --csv <arbitrary path>` loads a single loader from any location, gated, with no fixture fallback. It is per-loader rather than per-chain, so a full reference load is several invocations, but it is CORRECT where the chain verb is not. That also bounds the item: the contract to copy already exists and is one verb away, so this is two commands being made to agree, not an interface to design. MERGED 2026-08-13 (targeted groom) from Idea-119, whose own proposed disposition was to fold the five untested loaders into this item rather than file a coverage sweep. Read A5 for what it is: a DIRECT-IMPORT proxy, so fixture-driven and subprocess coverage do not show in it. Clause (d) therefore asks for an import-bearing test on the path this item changes, not for proof that a loader was untested in every sense. STANDING DIVERGENCE FOUND WHILE CONFIRMING IT, and it is load-bearing for any shared fixture: the producer convention is DOUBLE underscore (catalog_lobs__sample.csv), the company convention is SINGLE (catalog_lobs_sample.csv) -- confirmed by the SME. The same file therefore cannot serve both sides, and a file copied across is silently skipped rather than rejected. Record it in the port-prompt divergence ledger at this item.

G79Split refresh-reference by SOURCE — one command per subject, and wire the two loaders that belong to no chain at all
drydocs-loadP6taskp1opus / main
component-topology
depends on: G78

Acceptance: refresh-reference bundles SEVEN loaders across THREE unrelated sources with different natural refresh cadences. That bundle has no organising principle, which is why a loader can fall out of it and nothing notices. Split it so each command covers ONE source. (a) The split, by subject rather than by chain accident: the product catalog tier (catalog LOBs, product lines, products), the organisation tier (dev teams, team roles), and the business-application tier (applications, contacts). These are SEPARATE COMMANDS even where two share a source system, because the SME's cadence argument is per subject: business applications are not created daily, the operational estate can be. (b) WIRE THE TWO ORPHANS. pat_team_roles is gate-confirmed (C9, 2026-07-18), has a loader class and cypher, is reachable as `drydocs load pat_team_roles` -- and belongs to NO chain and NO profile, so no operator path has ever run it. area_products is in the same state. Either wire each into its subject command or record a written reason it is excluded; the one thing not allowed is the current silence. area_products has a plausible reason ready to be written down (lob-product-team.yaml records area_products: 0 with the standing area-product-missing open question); pat_team_roles has none that this item could find. (c) Cadence moves OFF the hand-assigned profile tuples and ONTO the source registry entry, so load_profile() DERIVES its steps by filtering on cadence instead of reading a literal maintained by hand. This is what makes "the source dictates how often it refreshes" true in code rather than true in a comment. (d) Acquisition mode joins it on the registry entry (file-drop | db-pull | api-pull | repo | scrape), so the anticipated CSV-to-database move for business-application data is a registry edit plus an adapter swap, with the loader, the command name, the sequence position and the cadence all unchanged. (e) PRESERVE ONE LOAD-ORDER INVARIANT ACROSS THE SPLIT, and state it where the split happens: seal_applications loads BEFORE any loader that can mint a :BusinessApplication. Producer satisfies it today by accident of chain order rather than by declaration, and the split is exactly when an accident gets lost. Producer is additionally safe because pat_product_mapping.cypher MERGEs on the SAME neutral app_id key seal_applications uses -- so no stub, no second node, no ordering dependency. The company is NOT safe: pat_app_links.cypher still MERGEs on the pre-S3 seal_id with is_stub=true, mints a null-app_id node the uniqueness constraint cannot match, and the subsequent SET collides (SME hit it live 2026-08-11; RELAY-8, a T23 residue). Once commands are keyed to sources, the constraint is expressible as a declared dependency rather than a position in a tuple -- state it that way, so the next reorder cannot silently break it. NAMING IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE -- this item splits and wires using CURRENT names. Renaming is GN1/GN2 and is frozen-and-ported as one unit; doing both at once makes an already wide port surface unreviewable.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) on SME direction. Depends on G78 because splitting a chain that silently skips its inputs just gives you more places to skip silently. The SME asked whether product and org structure can be separate commands while sharing sources -- yes, and that is the point: the COMMAND is keyed to the subject, the SOURCE is a property of the data, and two subjects may legitimately draw on one source system. What must not happen is the reverse, which is what exists now: one command spanning three sources, so nothing can say whether the command is complete. RIDER NOTE 2026-08-13 (targeted groom, from Idea-119): two of the five loaders named in G78 clause (d) are ones THIS split re-homes -- seal_contacts (a REFRESH_REFERENCE_CHAIN member) and business_segments (refreshed inside the same command, ahead of the chain tuple). If G78's coverage clause has not closed by the time this runs, the tests move WITH the loaders into their new subject command rather than being left pointing at a command that no longer exists.

C34dcat:theme — declare the EXISTING lob-product-team tree as a SKOS concept scheme and draft its gate, instead of minting a second subject vocabulary
ontologyP2taskp1opus / main
ontology-mapping

Acceptance: THE FINDING THAT SHAPES THIS ITEM, verified before it was raised rather than assumed: the hierarchy the SME proposed for subject classification -- LOB, Product Line, Product -- ALREADY EXISTS as config/taxonomy/lob-product-team.yaml (CatalogLOB > ProductLine > Product > DevTeam, B3, captured 2026-06-20), and the SME's vernacular examples are already ProductLine rows in it. This item does NOT mint a subject vocabulary; it declares the one that exists. (a) THE SKOS DECLARATION -- taxonomy, layer 1, NO gate, lands immediately. The file is a concept scheme in all but name: classification_only, hierarchical via parent_lob / parent_product_line, id-keyed, labelled. Declare it a skos:ConceptScheme with the parent links as skos:broader so dcat:theme has something standards-valid to point at. SKOS is already precedent in this very file, which cites skos:closeMatch for RECONCILES_TO. (b) THE GATE PROMPT, drafted not signed -- dcat:theme is a MEANING edge. It must pose: (b1) RESIDENCY, which BLOCKS the cross-corpus half. The design puts structured and unstructured context in TWO DATABASES, and a Neo4j relationship cannot span databases (Q8 -- the same constraint blocking G32's estate join), so one edge cannot reach one shared Concept from both sides. Three shapes: duplicate the scheme per database with identical concept IRIs; hold the scheme in one and carry the theme on the other as an IRI-valued PROPERTY joined application-side; or single database (ADR 0011). DECIDABLE NOW REGARDLESS, and the prompt says so: make the concept IRI the join key and keep it stable, so the vocabulary is portable whichever way residency rules and no work is stranded. (b2) IS a Product a skos:Concept, or does it HAVE one? ProductLine and Product are business entities with owners, teams and applications; dual-typing them is legal RDF and muddies what the node is. The alternative is a concept per product with skos:exactMatch. Rule it -- do not let a loader decide by accident. (b3) ANNOTATION DEPTH is the real control on grain: annotate at ONE level and derive the rest by skos:broader, so tagging a folder at Product yields its ProductLine and LOB free. That stops a deep vocabulary from multiplying annotations, and it beats capping vocabulary size, which forces a lie the moment the business genuinely has more rows than the cap. (b4) THE CARDINALITY ASK IS PREMATURE AT THE TIER NAMED, and the prompt must say why rather than silently declining. The SME asked for a limit under 5 at the AreaProduct level; lob-product-team.yaml records area_products: 0 and carries a STANDING OPEN QUESTION (area-product-missing) on whether that tier applies outside production PAT at all. Rule the tier before capping it. What CAN be ruled now is the ANNOTATION cap -- how many themes one subject may carry -- enforced as a DETECTOR, not a schema constraint, because a folder carrying six themes is evidence the folder does too much or the tagger hedged, and that is a finding worth reading rather than a write to refuse. (c) UNCLASSIFIED IS FIRST-CLASS, and out-of-scope is a DIFFERENT value from not-yet- classified. External-vendor and unrelated pages are permanently out of scope; an unclassified internal page is pending. Collapsing them makes coverage unmeasurable, because the number stops distinguishing backlog from scope. Same discipline as resource_pool.classify returning unknown with no label and a WARN. No graph writes, no ratification: the scheme declaration ships, the edge is the gate's.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 from an SME design session that began on Idea-105 and opened a second thread. THE ORIGINAL INTENT: folder-level runbooks are >90% automatable, and the roll-up axis was going to be "Data Series" -- an entity that is not commonly defined. Teams think in source name instead, which is why the existing ProductLine tier fits: it is both the vernacular people already use AND already captured. The roll-up therefore falls out of the concept scheme without Data Series ever being defined, which is the part to protect in review. WHY IT REACHES THE CONTEXT GRAPH (SME observation, and it is right): a theme is a PROJECTION AXIS, so "everything in this subject, right now" becomes a layer-4 slice instead of needing a new entity to hang it on. Themes are multi-valued by nature, so a process serving two subjects appears in both slices with nothing duplicated -- which a single Data Series field could never have done. SCOPE FENCE: declares and drafts. Does not populate real values (Internal), does not write the edge, does not build UI.

G77One theme vocabulary, two corpora: dcat:theme on the Control-M folder block AND the scraped-document envelope, joined by concept IRI
drydocs-coreP6taskp2opus / main
component-topology
depends on: C34 G84

Acceptance: One vocabulary classifies BOTH corpora -- that is the point, and it is what ties the structured estate to the unstructured one. (a) CONTROL-M, folder scope: a THEME token inside the DD1| folder block (guidelines section 7.5), registered in TOKEN_REGISTRY like any other token, multi-valued on the documented inner separator, values checked against the concept scheme with an unrecognised value RETURNED as a finding rather than raised -- the standing aliases-suggest / values-decide discipline. This is the folder-level block C29 originally intended for a Data Series roll-up that was never commonly defined. (b) SCRAPED DOCUMENTS: the same field on the document metadata envelope. The two-corpus architecture already rules that the vendor and Confluence corpora stay EPISTEMICALLY SEPARATE and merge only through a shared metadata envelope -- a theme is exactly such a field, which is why it fits rather than being bolted on. THE DISCIPLINE THAT MUST BE WRITTEN DOWN OR SOMEONE WILL BUILD PAST IT: the join is at the CLASSIFICATION, never the content. A document and a folder sharing a theme are both ABOUT that subject; that is not an assertion that the document describes the folder, and no edge may imply it. Trust tiers do not merge because two things share a subject. (c) The unclassified / out-of-scope split from C34 (c) is implemented on the scraper side, where it actually bites, and coverage reports the two apart. (d) Joined by CONCEPT IRI, never by label -- so this item works unchanged under one database or two, and label drift between corpora cannot fork the join. Zero graph writes: the field, its validation and the coverage split. The edge waits on C34.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 with C34, same session. Depends on C34 because a theme field populated against an undeclared scheme is free text with a schema-shaped name. DELIBERATELY NOT RAISED YET: the SME-facing classification UI, which the session described as possibly two pages. Building a classification surface before C34 rules residency and the Product-vs-Concept typing is the O59 mistake in a new place -- a widget built against a shape that turns out otherwise is thrown away. It grooms once C34 signs, and the two-page question then answers itself from the residency ruling rather than from taste. RAISED AT THE 2026-08-12 GROOM, and the reason depends_on grew: clause (a) reads a THEME token "inside the DD1| folder block", and nothing in the parser knows what that block is. G84 builds the block gate; this item registers a token on top of it. Without the dependency, two sessions implement the same sentinel differently in one file.

Acceptance: DETERMINISTIC FIRST, AGENT SECOND (user direction 2026-08-12): every remediation decision stays with the rules engine and the xml_io post-conditions; the agent never decides. It answers "why is this the rule?" and "does the vendor actually say that?" beside the SME diff, walking the three tiers that are ALREADY the ratified precedence order (CLAUDE.md section 4) -- (1) VENDOR: what BMC says the object is, from external/orchestration/bmc-controlm/ (the BASELINE); (2) PLATFORM STANDARDS APPLIED: how knowledge/standards/ + the R1-R28 rules registry refine it; (3) TEAM: who owns the thing being changed (LOB->Product->Team, SEAL/escalation routing). So the surface is a visualization of the existing precedence chain, not a new concept. HARD REQUIREMENTS: (a) every answer cites its corpus doc AND its trust level -- an answer sourced from a [GROUNDED search-snippets-only] capture (e.g. the XML-definition stub) must say so, never present it as vendor ground truth (the SOURCE-MANIFEST trust ladder is the contract); (b) read-only, no graph write -- consistent with the remediation module invariant; (c) precomputed material rides the generated-artifact pattern; a live agent call is its own seam, never a QuerySpec; (d) the FULL BMC scrape is loaded first -- declared as this feature's substrate in drydocs_remediation/module-requirements.md section 3, with the 403- blocked fetch list re-run from a network that reaches documents.bmc.com. GATED BEHIND the fix-diff surface existing (it reviews a diff; without one it reviews nothing). Precedents: the Q&A console for the answer surface; docmeta for citation handling.

Notes: Groomed from the 2026-08-12 user follow-up ("an agent query against the verified bmc documentation, to show vendor, then the platform standards applied, then the team"). Scope-noted as its own epic slice, larger than the defect fixes it rode in with; most useful once a real (non-demo) fix diff exists to review beside it.
