G92File-op operands are parsed from RAW shell text, so a variable path and its resolved twin become two different data assets — resolve the job's scope chain before the file-op parse
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G14 G46 G60

Acceptance: REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only, no database (J18): the G60 pre/post pass calls parse_command(value) on the RAW variables-CSV var_value, and _file_op keys the asset as asset_id(_FILE_OP_ASSET_KIND, location) from that verbatim operand -- so a job whose POSTCMD moves "%%R_PATH/out.dat" and a job whose CMD_LINE moves "/data/r/out.dat" plan edges to TWO DataAsset nodes for ONE file. The CMD_LINE pass has the same defect; only the pre/post pass makes it visible, because pre/post text is where the variable forms concentrate. (a) RESOLVE, THEN PARSE. The extractor builds the job's folder -> job scope chain and runs the shell text through the ONE resolver (drydocs_core/orchestration/controlm/resolve_layers / resolve_command_line, whose stated guardrail is "no caller may re-implement substitution"), then parses the RESOLVED text. No second substitution engine, no regex twin, no local %%-stripping helper -- a new substitution path in this extractor fails this item outright. (b) RAW STAYS BESIDE RESOLVED, never replaced -- the G46 derived-fact shape. The candidate carries both the verbatim operand and the resolved location, so a wrong binding is auditable rather than baked in. (c) CANONICAL RESIDUE IS NOT A FAILURE. {ODATE}-class tokens survive resolution by design and stay symbolic in the operand; they are counted as EXPECTED residue, distinct from an unresolved user variable, which is counted as a miss. Neither is dropped (the coverage house rule). (d) COUNT THE RESOLUTION QUALITY on the ResolveCoverage precedent (drydocs/cmdline_staging.py): per-run counters for resolved / residue / nothing-to-substitute / no-scope-chain, reported through the existing ExtractCoverage summary line so the yield is measurable in the same place the prepost_* counters already land. (e) SCOPE CHAIN COMES FROM THE SAME CSV the shell text does. The aliased projection carries var_scope (FOLDER | JOB); the raw export does not, and there the folder rows are the header row where JOB_NAME equals the folder name (the drydocs/staging.py is_folder_header rule). Both shapes must feed the chain, and a row with NO resolvable scope chain is counted, never silently parsed raw. ENDPOINTS AND MEANING ARE UNCHANGED: same READS_FROM / WRITES_TO, same ControlMJob -> DataAsset shape from the 2026-07-15/16 gate EDIT, no new relationship type, m3_reads_from / m3_writes_to stay planned. Zero graph writes; a unit test on a sample job proves the resolved and raw spellings of one path converge on ONE asset id.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-112, raised working through the G60 result with the user. Verified at the groom rather than taken from the entry: _prepost_pass parses var_value directly (controlm_inventory.py), resolve_layers / resolve_command_line already return each definition's resolved_value plus substitution provenance (G46, done), and PRECMD/POSTCMD are themselves SETVAR definitions -- so the scope chain that resolves the rest of the job resolves them in place. This is a FEED change, not a new parser and not a new resolver, which is why it is sonnet: every semantic decision it depends on was made at G14, G46 and G60. MODULE: drydocs-lineage, chosen because the change point is the extractor's pass; core's resolver is CALLED, not modified. If core turns out to need a public helper for the scope-chain assembly, that is a drydocs-core follow-up item, not a widening of this one.

G93A finished remediation batch reports no numbers — carry the run's counts into the Jira fix-package explanation through the run-log contract
drydocs-remediationP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only (J18): render_handoff() emits Findings, Scope, Change, Equivalence evidence, Acceptance and Rollback -- and not one count of what the run actually processed. The reviewer reading the ticket cannot tell whether the batch examined nine jobs or nine hundred, so "we fixed it" carries no denominator. Meanwhile the extractors already model exactly this (ExtractCoverage.summary() with the G60 prepost_* source split, XmlDefsCoverage, findings counted by rule) -- the pattern exists, the handoff just never reads it. (a) THE COUNTS RIDE THE RUN LOG, NOT THE CONSOLE. A remediation batch opens a LoaderRunLog (drydocs_core/run_log.py) and closes it with its counts in the summary, the same contract the loaders already use; the handoff is rendered FROM that recorded summary. Console output is a view of the run, never its record. (b) NUMBERS ARE RECORDED, NOT RECOMPUTED AT RENDER TIME. HandoffPackage carries the run's counts as data; render_handoff stays a pure deterministic template (the module's existing house rule). A test proves the rendered body reports the recorded numbers even when the finding list handed to the renderer is a subset -- otherwise the explanation silently re-derives a denominator from whatever survived filtering. (c) WHAT THE SECTION CARRIES, at minimum: objects examined, objects changed, findings by rule id and by severity, the ratified / unratified split (a warn-only finding must not inflate a fix count), and anything skipped WITH ITS REASON -- unparseable is counted, never dropped. (d) ABSENCE IS EXPLICIT. A package assembled without a run summary renders the section as not recorded rather than omitting it, so a missing measurement never reads as a clean run. (e) IT DOES NOT RESTATE THE EQUIVALENCE PROOF. proven / compared jobs stay in their own section with the three-valued PASS / DIVERGED / NOT PROVEN verdict; coverage counts what the run looked at, the proof states what it demonstrated, and merging them would let a big denominator read as evidence. Zero graph writes. No new relationship type, no vocabulary entry, no gate.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-113, user direction the same day. Verified at the groom: render_handoff has no counts section, and nothing under drydocs_remediation/ imports run_log at all today (drydocs/cli.py is the only LoaderRunLog caller) -- so the batch-side run log is part of this item, not an assumed prerequisite. MODULE: drydocs-remediation, chosen because both change points (jira.py, the batch entry point) are there; drydocs_core/run_log.py is ADOPTED unchanged. If the run-log contract itself needs a field it does not have, that is a drydocs-core follow-up, not this item. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the support -> dev handoff of the runbook automation use case. The ticket is where a support engineer's evidence becomes a developer's instruction, and an explanation without counts cannot be audited later against the run that produced it.

G94Which standard does a job validate against? A selection resolver on job type, job role and ETL engine — and an executable proof that the DD version digit never selects one
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G84

Acceptance: Today the token set is selected by ONE dimension: required_tokens(JobType) over FILE_WATCHER / PUBLISHER / BOTH. User direction 2026-08-12 rules the real selection a DECISION TREE -- a FileWatcher validates against the FileWatcher standard; a COMMAND job selects on its ETL ENGINE FIRST (DPL, Ab Initio, Informatica -- names the launcher registry already classifies as invocation_type DPL / ABINITIO / INFORMATICA) and falls back to a GENERIC standard carrying only the shared tokens (the DevX project key, the EMAIL_DL contacts) when no engine is identified. (a) ONE FUNCTION, ONE ANSWER: a selector takes the derived TASKTYPE, the registered JOB_ROLE token and the launcher classification, and returns a STANDARD IDENTITY plus the token set that identity requires. Selection is separated from validation -- validate() keeps taking what it is given, so the tree can be re-ruled without touching the parser. (b) THE GUARDRAIL BECOMES A TEST, which is the point of the item: guidelines section 7.5 and G84 clause (c) rule the DD digit a grammar VERSION that MUST NOT select a template or a standard. A test asserts that the SAME job under "DD1|" and under a hypothetical "DD2|" selects the SAME standard, so the next person who reaches for the version slot as a selector reds a guard instead of shipping it. (c) THE ENGINE BRANCH IS DECLARED, NOT INVENTED. Per-engine standards get their identity and their branch; the CONTENT of each engine's token set is NOT ruled here -- an engine with no ruled set inherits the generic set and REPORTS that it did, so an unruled engine is visible rather than silently generic. Inventing per-engine required tokens in this item is out of scope and fails it. (d) THE GENERIC SET IS DERIVED, NOT RETYPED: it is the shared subset already carried in the registry (JobType.BOTH plus the FOLDER_VARIABLES entries), so it cannot drift from TOKEN_REGISTRY. (e) UNSELECTABLE IS AN ANSWER. A job whose engine cannot be classified and whose job role is absent returns the generic standard WITH a reason, and coverage counts the reasons -- the adoption-not-compliance measure G84 established. Zero graph writes; every token stays proposed; no relationship-vocabulary entry and no property term is touched. Storage of the selected standard is explicitly NOT here -- see G95.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-12 (targeted groom) from Idea-114, clause 1 (the decision tree). Verified at the groom: config/launcher-registry.yaml already emits DPL / ABINITIO / INFORMATICA invocation types through classify_executable(), so the engine dimension needs no new classifier; JOB_ROLES is already the C30 discriminator set (PUBLISHER / PLACEMENT / TRUST_INGEST); and required_tokens() is currently keyed on JobType alone, which is the gap. depends_on G84 because the selector must read the population and the version the sentinel parse produces, and G84 is where both were built. WHY THIS HALF IS BUILDABLE AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT: choosing WHICH standard applies is derivable from data the repo already has. Choosing WHERE a standard lives, what its id is, and whether a team may hold its own profile is a contract change to the parse contract -- that is G95, and it goes to the gate first.

G95Draft the gate prompt for standard IDENTITY and its carrier: can a validation profile be stored per team, and what may legitimately select a standard?
configP6taskp3fable / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A gate prompt is DRAFTED -- drafting decides nothing (the G27 / W1 / N10 / G61 precedent), nothing is written to the graph, and no entry leaves `planned` until the SME signs. The prompt must put four questions, each with the evidence already in the repo: (a) IDENTITY: does a standard get a stable id, and what is its shape? Today the per-job-type sets are CODE-AS-DATA in TOKEN_REGISTRY, whose own docstring calls itself "the single source both the parser and the published register read from, so code and document cannot drift" -- guarded by the registry-vs-standard agreement test. Giving a standard an id outside that module is a CONTRACT CHANGE and the prompt must say so plainly, with what the agreement test would then be guarding. (b) CARRIER: user direction 2026-08-12 proposes a config table (SQLite was floated) keyed by standard id, holding a validation profile BY TEAM, with a platform / product hierarchy later. The prompt lays the candidate carriers side by side -- versioned YAML under config/ (the launcher-registry precedent: schema-pinned, test-guarded, teams add rows without a code change) versus a database table -- against what each costs at review time and at port time, and asks the SME to rule. It does not pre-pick one. (c) WHAT MAY SELECT A STANDARD, restated as a fence rather than assumed: section 7.5 and G84 rule the DD digit a grammar VERSION and forbid it selecting a template or a standard, so a standard id needs its OWN carrier. The prompt asks the SME to ratify that fence explicitly, because a per-team registry is exactly the pressure that would break it. (d) DIVERGENCE POLICY: if a team may hold its own profile, what may it change? Adding a team-local token is the C16 annotation case the parser already knows; RELAXING a required token of the company standard is a governance decision, and the prompt must ask whether that is permitted at all, and if so who ratifies it. Every term or entry the prompt proposes is registered `planned` and stays planned until the gate signs. The deliverable is the prompt file plus its gate-log stub -- no code, no registry, no schema.

Promoting the DRAFT rather than the build is the standing pattern -- a prompt decides nothing, and it puts the question in front of the SME with the evidence attached instead of leaving it as an inbox line nobody can act on. U21IMPORTS edges are never retracted, so fan-in inflates permanently and test debt under-reports — the code-snapshot load sweeps nodes but not edges
drydocs-loadP16bugp1sonnet / main
self-documentation

Acceptance: After a `drydocs load-code-snapshot` run, the graph's IMPORTS edges EQUAL the loaded snapshot's IMPORTS edges for every module that snapshot CONTAINED. Today they do not, and the edge only ever grows. THE DEFECT, reproduced 2026-08-13 (desktop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB) against the graph freshly reloaded from that day's snapshot: `drydocs/loaders/seal_attribution.py` still carries an IMPORTS edge to `drydocs/loaders/base.py`; the file contains ZERO occurrences of the string "base" (K8 removed the import at 4df4df2) and the snapshot records no such edge. The edge SURVIVED a full re-run, so this is not staleness and a refresh does not fix it. Size at that reading: 985 live IMPORTS edges against 982 in the snapshot -- three ghosts, one of which put `loaders/base.py` at fan-in 32 where the tree says 31, i.e. it distorts the repo's most-cited change-risk metric. A5 is affected in the DANGEROUS direction: a module whose test import was DELETED keeps the ghost edge and still counts as tested, so test debt reads better than it is. THE FIX. (a) PER-SOURCE RETRACTION, NEVER A GLOBAL DELETE. For each module the loaded snapshot INCLUDED, the edges this loader wrote that the snapshot no longer asserts are retracted; edges touching a module the snapshot did NOT include are untouched, and edges written by any other loader are untouched. The scoping discipline already exists one file away -- base.py's D7 mark pass refuses to run without either `full_extract` or a scope property, logging why -- and this clause is that discipline applied to relationships. (b) DECIDE AND RECORD: marked or deleted. The node half MARKS (removed_from_source_at + removed_by_run_id) rather than deleting, which is what makes U13's "every query pack filters tombstones" rule necessary. Whichever this item picks, it states the reason, and if edges are marked then the read paths that consume IMPORTS (the tech-debt skill's A3/A5 queries, the review-plan seed queries) filter them the same way U13 made node queries filter -- a tombstoned edge that no query excludes is the same defect wearing a property. (c) THE COUNT IS REPORTED, never silent: edges retracted (and reactivated, if marked) appear in the load summary beside nodes_marked_removed, per the STG_PARSE_QUALITY house rule the node pass already follows. (d) GUARDS, both of them: loading snapshot A (edge present) then snapshot B (edge absent for a module B contains) leaves no live edge; and loading a snapshot that OMITS a module entirely leaves that module's edges alone. The first proves the sweep works, the second proves it cannot over-reach. (e) VERIFY ON THE REAL GRAPH at close, venue named per J18: live IMPORTS count equals the newest snapshot's, the seal_attribution -> base ghost is gone, and the A3 top fan-in is RE-MEASURED rather than re-typed.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-13 (targeted groom -- node labels and Cypher loaders) from Idea-118. SAME FAMILY AS U13, one grain down: the D7 sweep tombstones removed MODULES and nothing sweeps removed EDGES, so the import graph is append-only by construction. The repo holds exactly one edge-retraction precedent -- `drydocs/loaders/cypher/stale_edge_cleanup.cypher` (D1: delete condition edges for changed jobs before re-asserting them) -- and a grep of the tracked tree on 2026-08-13 finds NO live caller for it, so the pattern exists as a file rather than as a mechanism. Worth reading it anyway: it is the shape (scope to the keys this run touched, delete, re-assert) this item generalizes. MODULE drydocs-load: the change is in the loader and its Cypher, not in the depgraph instrument -- the snapshot is CORRECT, the load is what never subtracts. PAIRS WITH U22, found in the same session and from the same cross-check (the loaded graph vs the snapshot it was loaded from): U22 detects a load that never RAN, this fixes a load that runs and never RETRACTS. Neither substitutes for the other -- U22's freshness check would have reported this graph as current, because it was.

U22The code graph can go stale for weeks and nothing says so: compare the graph's newest last_seen_at against the newest snapshot's captured_at

Acceptance: THE INCIDENT, 2026-08-13 (desktop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB): every :CodeModule carried `last_seen_at = 2026-08-02T23:06:42Z` from ONE run id -- loaded once on Aug 2, never refreshed, ELEVEN DAYS. The session read A3's top fan-in as 28, which is the Aug-2 value (the tech-debt skill's own baselines run 28 -> 29 on 08-04 -> 31 on 08-09), and it looked current. Same class as G78: not a failed read, a read that SUCCEEDED with the wrong data, sitting underneath every architecture and debt decision. `drydocs load-code-snapshot` repairs it in one command; nothing COMPARES the graph against the snapshot series. (a) THE COMPARISON EXISTS AS CODE, not as a habit: max(:CodeModule.last_seen_at) in the drydocs database against the newest `knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/drydocs-*.json` meta.captured_at, reporting the drift, the run id that last loaded, and WHICH snapshot it compared -- so "the graph is current" is falsifiable rather than assumed. (b) WARN, NOT FAIL -- ruled at this groom, and the reason is the argument CLAUDE.md already makes for snapshot.ps1's CI check: recording repo structure and passing a gate are unrelated jobs, and this check must never block a suite run or a snapshot on a machine with no database. It surfaces where the wrong number was actually consumed -- the tech-debt skill's read path -- and may ALSO ride the session ritual beside the CI check; the item states where it put it and why. (c) THE UNIT-TESTABLE HALF IS THE COMPARISON, not the freshness: a test drives it over fixtures -- fresh, stale, no snapshot on disk, empty graph, database unreachable -- and asserts each verdict, so the mechanism is guarded on a machine with no database. tests/unit/test_code_graph_review_plan.py is the offered home (it already fails when the typed package allow-list and pyproject.toml disagree, so the shape is there); a different home is fine with the reason written down. (d) DATABASE-UNREACHABLE IS A DISTINCT VERDICT, never "fresh". The failure this item exists to stop is a check that reports green because it could not look. OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: auto-running the load. A stale graph is REPORTED, never silently refreshed -- a check that repairs what it measures can never be trusted to have measured anything.

The likely code home straddles them -- a unit test file the docs items also touch -- which is exactly why the subject and not the file decided it. U23Nothing joins a loader to the Cypher it executes — draft the gate rider for a loader-to-cypher-file edge, the .cypher nodes that carry zero edges

Acceptance: A gate rider is DRAFTED and nothing else. Drafting decides nothing (the G27 / W1 / N10 / G95 precedent): no vocabulary entry leaves `planned`, no edge is written, and if the gate does not sit, the drafted rider IS the deliverable. VIA THE GATE is the whole point -- a new relationship type is an ontology decision under CLAUDE.md section 6, never an import convenience. It carries four things. (a) THE FACT, RE-MEASURED rather than copied from the 2026-08-02 note that raised it: `drydocs/loaders/` holds .py loaders, their .cypher files and their .sql side by side; the .cypher files are :CodeModule nodes with NO edges at all, while each loader names its Cypher as a literal path in Python (the CYPHER_DIR / "<name>.cypher" idiom). The prompt states the current counts and the date it counted them. (b) THE EDGE QUESTION, put as a question: what does the edge MEAN -- "executes", "reads as a resource", something narrower -- and does the .sql beside it carry the same edge or a different one? Direction, cardinality, and whether one label with a role property beats two labels (the documented RUNS_ON-overload risk is the standing worked example on this side). (c) THE EMITTER, because the edge has nowhere to come from today: the depgraph scanner does not emit it, so the prompt says where it would -- a static read of the CYPHER_DIR literal, in the instrument (the sibling repo, which means an expected_commit bump) or in the loader that reads the snapshot -- and what each costs. This is the clause that stops the rider being signed with no path to a first row. (d) WHAT IT UNLOCKS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT, stated plainly so the item is never judged against a promise it did not make: gate `self-documentation-code-graph` section H5 already records that :CodeModule to the OPERATIONAL graph -- "which module loads this Control-M job" -- is NOT delivered by that gate and needs a second item, precisely because the module-to-label mapping lives in the loaders' Cypher rather than in their imports. A loader-to-cypher edge is the FIRST half of that join and not the join; the prompt says so.

The emitter change the rider scopes is drydocs-load / graph-infra work and belongs to whatever item the gate produces, not to this one. p3 on the entry's own Low priority -- the nodes have sat edgeless since 2026-08-02 with no consequence beyond an unanswerable query, and the H5 question it feeds is not scheduled.

G97The m7 payload build: launcher and payload stop sharing the INVOKES fold — USES_ARTIFACT edges plus script_role and the artifact properties on :Script
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: NO GATE IS OPENED OR REOPENED -- this builds what two signed gates already ruled. cmdline-nfr-vetting (2026-07-21, SME-2 / SME-3) ruled the DISTINCT label rather than a single label with a role, and adopted the :Script refinements with it; rua-load-shapes (2026-08-07, 28/28, applied at G55) ACTIVATED m3_invokes and m7_uses_artifact in the same breath, on the stated reasoning that activating INVOKES alone would land payloads in the 1..n fold first and force an in-graph migration. G16's own notes name this item: "the m7 build (payload migration to USES_ARTIFACT, script_role stamping) is its own follow-up item once the writer endpoint work lands." (a) THE SPLIT: the writer emits USES_ARTIFACT from the job to the PAYLOAD artifact the launcher dispatches, while INVOKES keeps the LAUNCHER only. The discrimination comes from the G16 FACT_REGISTRY canonicals (ETL_ARTIFACT_URI / ETL_ARTIFACT_KIND / ETL_ARTIFACT_SHA and the ETL_PLATFORM pair) under the aliases-suggest-values-decide contract, plus the G15 launcher properties -- NEVER from a variable NAME alone, which is the 2,384-variable gap analysis' one durable finding: names lie. (b) :Script GAINS script_role {launcher, payload} and the gate-adopted artifact properties (platform / artifact_uri / artifact_kind / platform_flags / script_path). The property already exists -- the writer stamps script_role='profile' for the rua profile case (G23, section C2) -- so this EXTENDS a value set rather than inventing a property. Script identity stays PATH-keyed; that ruling is not touched. (c) ENDPOINT CLASS PER EDGE: to_node is Script | ETLProcess per rua-load-shapes section B2 -- one edge meaning, two endpoint classes, the endpoint RECORDED on the edge -- with the raw evidence string (the command line or variable form that produced it) kept VERBATIM per section B3, which is what keeps the endpoint choice re-checkable later. (d) EXISTING GRAPHS: state the position rather than assume a clean load. Where a live graph already folded payloads into a 1..n INVOKES set, either an idempotent re-load (MERGE-keyed) or a named migration step covers it -- whichever, it is written down and the counts are reported. A silent double-representation (payload on both labels) is the one outcome that must be impossible. (e) COUNTS AND A WARN STREAM: invocations classified launcher, classified payload, and UNCLASSIFIED. An unclassified invocation stays exactly where it is today and is reported; it is never promoted to a payload on a guess. TESTS: a fixture command line carrying both a launcher and a payload yields exactly one INVOKES and one USES_ARTIFACT edge with script_role stamped on both endpoints; a payload-less command line yields no USES_ARTIFACT edge at all; the vocabulary guard (write_curated raises GateBoundVocabularyError on a non-active entry) still holds. Full suite green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-13 (targeted groom -- node labels and Cypher loaders) from Idea-23, whose parked trigger -- "once the writer's ETLProcess endpoint work makes the edge landable" -- has FIRED, verified two ways at the groom rather than assumed. (1) m7_uses_artifact is `status: active` in drydocs_core/ontology/relationship_vocabulary/40-local-scheduler.yaml, activated 2026-08-07, where the inbox entry recorded it as `planned`. (2) drydocs_lineage/writer.py MERGEs :ETLProcess on its token and carries the union-endpoint machinery, so the endpoint class the edge needs exists. ALSO VERIFIED ABSENT, so this is a real build and not a re-close: the writer emits NO USES_ARTIFACT edge today and stamps script_role only for the rua profile case -- a grep of writer.py on 2026-08-13 returns the profile stamp and nothing else. RELATED: G23 (the curated rua load this extends), G55 (the activation), G16 (the fact feed), G12 (which already lands INVOKES on :ETLProcess for the wrapper-payload expansion and is the precedent for clause (c)).

N12Declare every registry dataset's ACQUISITION PATH: manual drops name their format + landing-zone directory, automated pulls name api-or-db
configP11taskp2sonnet / pipeline-config
source-column-mappings

Acceptance: Every DATASET row in config/source-registry.yaml carries a first-class `acquisition:` block stating HOW the data arrives, replacing today's smear across three half-fields that do not compose into an answer (`adapter` -- csv/oracle/yaml/markdown/json, 8 rows carrying `~`; `connector` -- doc corpora only; `locator` -- free-shape, each source inventing its own key). (a) `mode: manual | automated` on EVERY dataset row, including the `adapter: ~` ones: the build CLASSIFIES the existing rows, it does not add the field only to new ones. That per-row classification IS the payoff -- "what is still hand-fed?" becomes a query instead of an audit. (b) MANUAL rows carry `format: csv | ascii | json` plus `drop_dir:`, whose COMMITTED value is the landing-zone CONVENTION -- DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT-relative, the `controlm-xml/` precedent, resolved by drydocs_core/data_root.py. The real directory lives ONLY in the internal twin (the `locator.extract: ~` discipline, unchanged): no real path, host or share name is ever committed (Scan D / J27 class). (c) AUTOMATED rows carry `via: api | db` plus the pull's coordinates BY REFERENCE, never restated -- for `db` the row's own dataset id already names the qualified object ({origin}@{db}.{schema}.{table}); for `api` the row names the CALL SURFACE, with the G96 Control-M adapter (drydocs_core/adapters/controlm/api.py) as the worked example. (d) ENFORCEMENT IS THE TEST, NOT THE SCHEMA. config/schemas/source-registry.schema.json is shape-only and permissive by design (S6 -- no `additionalProperties: false`), so a block added to the YAML alone would validate silently. The schema DECLARES the block (enums + the conditional required keys) and tests/unit/test_source_registry.py is what FAILS: every dataset row has `acquisition`; manual implies `format` + `drop_dir`; automated implies `via`; and a committed `drop_dir` that is absolute or otherwise escapes the landing-zone convention fails the boundary check. (e) SCOPE FENCE -- config/source-registry.yaml DATASET rows only. SYSTEM rows are unchanged, and the doc corpora in config/doc-source-registry.yaml are OUT of scope here (they already carry `connector:`); extending the field to that ledger is a separate call. (f) `mode: manual` IS THE EXPECTED FIRST STATE, NEVER A DEFECT (SME framing 2026-08-18): every new source has an exploratory phase -- profiling, ontology work, mapping, trial Neo4j loads -- and a .csv or .json file is the natural manual loader for it. The field RECORDS where a source sits in that lifecycle (manual exploratory -> automated productionized), so no test, report or render may present `manual` as a violation or as debt to be eliminated. (g) TWO FENCES. This item RECORDS mode -- it builds NO watcher, mover or copier for the drop directories. And it does NOT rule the FLIP (who flips manual -> automated, on what evidence, and how that relates to the override -> source-corrected flip): that ruling is N13's, via the gate. Full suite green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-18 from Idea-133 (SME ask the same day), with the exploratory-phase framing supplied in-session. Idea-132 is the live driver: the ServiceNow extracts are moving hand-pulled-CSV -> SQL over the replica, and TODAY that transition has no field to flip -- it shows up only as prose in `notes:`. Idea-115 caught this class once already (the rua copy path existed only as a derived expression; the fix was to make both ends name each other). MODULE/PHASE/EPIC follow N10, which pins exactly this combination for registry-schema work (the v2 registry is N7/N9's artifact); agent pipeline-config per its config layer. HITL-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION: this adds a config field recording an operational fact -- no edge is created, no relationship meaning changes -- and the field itself is SME-directed (2026-08-18), the J23 pre-decided-ruling precedent. THREE AXES, ONE ROW, ALL DIFFERENT: `confirmed` = semantic gate sign-off; the wired/ready flag N10 proposes = pipeline-wiring readiness; `acquisition.mode` = how the data physically arrives. If N10's gate signs, the two fields COMPOSE on the same row -- neither subsumes the other -- and whichever lands second says so in the registry header. Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop) from the 2026-08-05 IDEAS entries. THIS RUNS BEFORE THE GATE, not after: "about two hundred accounts per application" is the estimate the gate cannot rule on, and the census turns it into "N of ~200, and here is what the other rows are". The §Q0 disagreement breakdown is the part that decides whether the directory is a trustworthy ownership source with expected consumer divergence, or a lagging record needing remediation — a question raised only after the gate was drafted, which is why it sits in a separate item rather than inside the gate page. module: config (a source-scoping measurement, not a loader). Producer-side this repo carries the METHOD; the counts themselves are Internal. PRODUCER HALF DELIVERED 2026-08-07 (laptop), and the item is BLOCKED rather than done because its acceptance asks for real counts this repo structurally cannot produce — it holds no directory extract, which is the whole point of the demand-set pull. Shipped: drydocs/fid_census.py (pure — opens no file, contacts no database, writes nothing; every input injected), tests/unit/test_fid_census.py (14 tests, all synthetic), and docs/k16-fid-census-company-prompt.md following the 2026-08-07 company-pack convention. Doc 09 gains a "The numbers" table with every cell marked pending, and an explicit note that an empty cell means NOT MEASURED, never zero. TWO DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE COUNTS ARRIVE. (1) COUNTS-ONLY IS ENFORCED BY THE RETURN TYPE, not by discipline: FidCensus holds int and dict[str,int] fields only, so a row dump is UNEXPRESSIBLE, and a test pins that structurally. That is what lets the result travel back into this repo at all — a later field carrying account names would leak Internal values into a producer-side artifact. (2) THE §G5 READING IS NEVER COMPUTED. The gate says the three readings are distinguished per case and never globally, with a human ruling each — so the census counts disagreements mechanically and parks every one in `unruled` until an SME ruling is injected. The number still sitting in `unruled` is itself reportable: the never-silent rule applied to the report rather than to a load. THE BLOCKER'S REASON CHANGED 2026-08-12 (SME evidence) — still blocked, much smaller ask. The FID directory is not an external system needing an export or an onboarding: it is `psgmgr.HR_PHONE_EXP`, functional rows `EMP_TYP_CD = 'FCT'`, in the replica ALREADY IN SCOPE and already the Control-M source. So the census is a SINGLE-SCHEMA JOIN — demand set (i) from CM_DEF_VJOB.OWNER against the directory in the same schema — and no new source crosses the boundary. Status stays blocked because the counts are Internal and this repo has no psgmgr access, which is unchanged; what changed is that satisfying it no longer waits on a source onboarding, only on someone running the query company-side. RUN Q6 FIRST (gate fid-identity-and-scope): whether CM_DEF_VJOB.OWNER holds the NAME or the ID decides the join key, and the two keys give different demand sets. Measuring with the wrong one produces a confident wrong number. module: config is kept as the WORK AREA; the code module classifies as drydocs-review in test_module_boundary.py (it loads nothing and configures nothing — it produces the counts an SME rules from, the same reasoning that puts source_mappings there).

Acceptance: A platform app code can no longer be mistaken for a tier-1 code by either route. (a) DERIVATION: tier comes from the folder name — prefix positions 3-5 matched against the closed platform-code list (six codes; the list lives in the VALUES twin under internal/, the mechanism in the publishable twin) — so a code-level row that carries a SEAL is not read as an application attribution for folders that are merely HOSTED by that platform. A row-level test covers both a platform prefix and an application prefix. (b) AUTHORING: the mapping store gains an explicit platform-declaration entry kind (app_code + declaration + rationale) rather than the current declare-by-absence-of-app_id encoding. The store's app_id-required check STAYS — it is correct for tier-1 rows, and relaxing it would let a blank target through as an ordinary attribution. (c) Folders under a declared platform code that the steward has not resolved per-folder surface as `platform-unresolved` instead of falling through to the K2 fuzzy fallback, which is what K7 §B2 already rules and what the current write path cannot express. No graph-test relaxation: folder-attribution-coverage stays 1:1. Full suite green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop) from Idea-66 + Idea-69, with Idea-63b and Idea-68 riding as clauses. WHY (a) IS THE BIGGER HALF and was the surprise: this looked like a steward capture exercise until the SME supplied the DAT SRE Framework -> APPCODE table. The platform list is CLOSED AT SIX CODES and positions 3-5 of the folder prefix decide the tier, so tier assignment is MECHANICALLY DERIVABLE — a six-row list plus a name parse, not a data-entry backlog. It also means this item does NOT depend on the SME's owed tier-1/tier-2 enumeration (Idea-28): that enumeration is needed to RESOLVE a tier-2 code's consumers, not to recognize one. THE FAILURE IT PREVENTS IS SILENT AND LOOKS CORRECT. `AOC -> <platform SEAL>` is a TRUE statement about the platform and a false one about the consumer folders it would be stamped on. Both AOC (the datalake / Ab Initio platform) and DCL (the DPL launcher spine) are shared codes whose folders serve many consuming applications, and the only in-file hint of platform-ness is the word "Platform" in `descr` — the untrustworthy column. Nothing is mis-written TODAY only because no producer-side platform code has been authored yet. RIDER (Idea-63b): `descr` is a CORROBORATION signal with a known-imperfect base rate, never a validity test and never a derivation source. If this item compares column 2 to the head of column 3 at all, the output is a REVIEW QUEUE of disagreeing rows for a human — candidate stale renames, decommissioned SEALs, copy-paste — not a pass/fail gate. RIDER (Idea-68), cosmetic and do it here or not at all: "tier" names two things — the K7 row-kind (a STRING enum seal-born|platform|dual-coded) and the K2 match precedence (an INT, 1 SEAL .. 5 manual). The value spaces do not collide, so a `tier` edge property is not ambiguous in practice and this is naming hygiene rather than a correctness risk — but `row_kind` vs `match_tier` is worth renaming BEFORE either surfaces in a QuerySpec, and this item is already in both files. DISAGREEMENT RULE (added at claim, 2026-08-05): clause (a) gives the loader TWO tier signals for an authored code — the name-derived tier and the row's declared kind — and the acceptance did not say which wins when they disagree (e.g. a steward authors a tier-1 row for a code the name parse says is platform). Ruling, on the Idea-63b pattern and the S10 refusal precedent: a disagreement NEVER resolves silently. The name derivation wins for BLOCKING fan-out — a platform-prefixed code never fans out code-level even if its row claims tier-1 — and the disagreeing row lands in the review queue with both signals shown; a human re-authors or the list is corrected. The inverse disagreement (row declares platform, name parse says application) blocks nothing but queues the same way. DONE 2026-08-05 (desktop, 1386faf): (a) built — load_platform_codes (values twin internal/standards/technology/platform-codes.yaml, six codes; missing file = guard inert) + platform_prefix pos3-5 + the resolver guard (blocked fan-out queues a RowKindDisagreement, folders surface platform-unresolved; inverse queues without blocking); row-level tests cover a platform prefix AND an application prefix. (b) built — validate_app_code_row: platform code-level row now REQUIRES the platform's own app_id + rationale (declare-by-absence retired; legacy empty-app_id shape still reads as a declaration in the resolver, defensively); store schema v3. (c) built — declared-code folders already surfaced platform-unresolved; the guard now routes derived-platform codes there too. Idea-68 rider APPLIED: tier -> row_kind end to end (column, CSV header, wire, model, edge property, steward screen); K2 match tiers keep their name (no property surfaces, nothing to rename). Idea-63b rider NOT EXERCISED: no descr comparison was built (the rider is conditional; the review-queue rule stands recorded for whoever builds one). COMPANY-SIDE: header+edge-property renames ride the T23 migration family — their tier-authored rows re-author as row_kind; live r.tier edges migrate with the K8 reload. Suite 1597 green. K19 unblocks.

Acceptance: The store can answer "is this code's mapping older than the folders it is being applied to?" and says so where a steward will see it. Concretely: a check that reports any app_code whose mapping `authored_on` PREDATES the first-seen date of folders now carrying that code, as a review queue with counts — never an automatic re-attribution, because a reissued code and a genuinely growing application are indistinguishable without a human. Either effective dating on the mapping row (valid_from/valid_to) or the detection alone, with the choice recorded in the item's close note and the reason. A test builds the reuse case from fixtures: one code, two eras, folders on both sides.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-05 (desktop) from Idea-67 (user, same day). THE SOURCE FACT: a Control-M app code is a 3-character namespace, which is scarce, so codes are retired and REISSUED with a different meaning — `DDC` is the documented case (created for the PySpark conversion, repurposed, nothing PySpark now). That makes a code -> application mapping an as-of assertion, the same shape as the FID -> SEAL registration ruled in `fid-identity-and-scope` §B1 and the third current-state-only identifier found in one week. `authored_on` already gives the store an as-of; what nothing prevents is a reused code silently inheriting its predecessor's mapping while folders authored under the OLD meaning keep an attribution that is now wrong. DEPENDS ON K18 for a practical reason, not a logical one: K18 touches the same store entry shape, and doing the two in one pass avoids migrating the row format twice. NOT IN SCOPE: deciding whether history should be preserved (a retired mapping kept valid_to-stamped) or overwritten. That is an ontology-flavored question about whether the graph records past attributions at all, and it goes to a gate if the answer is anything but "detect and report".

K21LAPTOP: mine the ServiceNow replica screenshots into the TOM mapping — the working query, the view inventory, and whether we are asking the replica for the right columns
taxonomyP9taskp2fable / main
seal-attribution

Acceptance: THIS IS A LAPTOP ITEM by SME assignment — the evidence is a set of DBeaver screenshots held on the laptop, and they are INTERNAL: replica host, database name, schema names, SEAL application ids, configuration-item names and the `x_<scope>_` company scope prefix never enter this repo. Only mechanism is recorded here; anything value-bearing stays company-side. Three deliverables. (1) THE WORKING QUERY, transcribed as MECHANISM into the ServiceNow/TOM material: the join spine is `x_<scope>_cmdb_tom_main` -> `x_<scope>_cmdb_tom_roles` (role -> sys_id, active) -> `cmdb_ci` (parent_id) -> `core_company` -> `cmdb_ci_service_discovered` -> `sys_user_group` (group, and again on assignment_group) -> `cmdb_ci_business_app`, with the CI self-join on `inherited_from_ci`. The columns that matter to DryDocs are named and mapped to our vocabulary: `u_seal_application_id` / `u_seal_deployment_id` (the SEAL join), `correlation_id`, `sys_class_name`, `inheritance` / `inherited_from_ci`, `u_status`, `u_application_state`, `u_external_service`, and the role/group/team names. State which of those the TOM-role gates (G35, seal-tom-attribution-reshape) already assume and which are NEW evidence. (2) THE VIEW INVENTORY as taxonomy: the replica exposes one `V_`-prefixed view per ServiceNow table across several `DW_*_DATA_VIEW` schemas (a common/CMDB one, an ITSM one, and at least two others). Capture the view -> ServiceNow-table naming rule and the schema split; that rule is what keeps `origin: snow` unambiguous while the carrier is Snowflake, and it is currently asserted in a comment with nothing behind it. (3) THE PRECISION QUESTION, which is the point of the item rather than a rider: the sample query is a hand-built REPORT — it filters to one company, one application state set, one SEAL id and one named CI. That is not an ingestion contract. Decide what DryDocs should actually pull, and justify it against the PUBLIC ServiceNow CMDB documentation (the tables are stock ServiceNow, so their canonical columns, `sys_class_name` hierarchy and CI-relationship model are all publicly documented and can be read from the web without touching the estate) — the vendor doc is the baseline, the replica is the instance, and where they disagree the difference is a company extension worth naming. Specifically rule whether the CI-relationship tables (`cmdb_rel_ci` and the `cmdb_rel_*` family visible in the navigator) belong in the pull, since a CMDB without its relationship rows is a node list rather than a graph. Output is an analysis document plus, if warranted, a DRAFT dataset row for the registry under the `snow@[db].[schema].<servicenow_table>` grammar with `confirmed: false`. NO source is activated, no loader is built and no gate is signed inside this item — a real pull scope is a gate decision.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-09 (desktop) on SME direction, from DBeaver screenshots of the replica the SME will query. WHY THE LAPTOP: the screenshots live there, and they are Internal — moving them to reach a different session is the wrong direction of travel. CONTEXT THIS ITEM DEPENDS ON, so it is not re-derived: ServiceNow metadata is NOT read from ServiceNow. It is read from an AWS Snowflake REPLICA, which is the same shape as Control-M being read from the Oracle `psgmgr` replica rather than from the orchestrator. So `snowflake` is the CARRIER and `snow` keeps the ORIGIN slot — recorded on both system entries in config/source-registry.yaml 2026-08-09 with guards, after the SME flagged SNOW/Snowflake as an IMPORTANT confusion. The v2 grammar already ruled this ("replica grammar: origin catalog, carrier snowflake"). WHY THE PUBLIC-DOC LEG IS WORTH THE TIME rather than shortcutting to the replica: these are STOCK ServiceNow tables, so the vendor documents the canonical schema publicly. That gives a baseline the estate cannot supply — it tells us which columns are ServiceNow's and which are local extensions (the `u_` prefix and the `x_<scope>_` scoped app are the two local classes visible in the sample), and a column we invent a meaning for because we only ever saw it in one hand-built report is exactly the kind of assumption T10/T13 exist to prevent. Route the vendor lookup through the reference-librarian agent and register what it finds in reference/REGISTRY.yaml, the same way BMC and Oracle are held. RELATIONSHIP TO THE OPEN TOM GATES: G35 (TOM-roles enumeration, in progress) and seal-tom-attribution-reshape both reason about role classes and cardinality from the SEAL side. This item supplies the ServiceNow-side evidence they have been arguing without — the `tom_roles` join and its `active` flag are the live shape of exactly what G35 is trying to enumerate. Feed the findings INTO those gates; do not pre-empt them. EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-08-09 (SME showed the cmdb_rel family live, so clause (3)'s relationship-table question is ANSWERED IN PART before the item starts — do not re-derive these, verify them): (a) THE EDGE TABLE IS REAL AND IS AN EDGE LIST. `cmdb_rel_ci` carries `parent` / `child` / `type`, all sys_id GUIDs, with `type` an FK to `cmdb_rel_type` — which in turn carries `name`, `child_descriptor` and an `end_point` boolean. That is a FORWARD LABEL plus an INVERSE LABEL on the type row, which is the same shape as this repo's own relationship_vocabulary (`neo4j_label` + `inverse_label`). The mapping is therefore close to mechanical rather than interpretive, and the item should say so rather than treating it as open. Also present: `connection_strength` and `percent_outage`, i.e. the CMDB models impact weight on the edge, which we have no equivalent for. (b) THE REPLICA IS NOT A PURE MIRROR, and this is the sharpest correction to the 'stock ServiceNow tables' premise the item is built on. The view carries columns ServiceNow never had: a `dwintel_dl_*` snapshot family (snapshot date, load timestamp, snapshot trim) and a `delete_flag`. Those are CARRIER artifacts of the data-lake replication, not vendor schema — exactly the vendor-baseline-vs-instance difference clause (3) exists to name, now with a concrete first example. (c) `delete_flag` MAKES SOFT DELETES AN INGESTION CONTRACT QUESTION, not a detail: if rows persist in the replica after deletion in ServiceNow, then any pull that ignores the flag ingests dead CIs and dead edges as live ones. Rule it explicitly. The D7 tombstone idiom is the obvious precedent — we already distinguish removed-from-source from never-existed, and this is the same problem arriving from a different source. (d) THE SERVICENOW AUDIT ENVELOPE IS PRESENT: `sys_created_by` / `sys_created_on` / `sys_updated_by` / `sys_updated_on` map cleanly onto the four frozen envelope property names, so a `config/audit-fields.yaml` entry for any snow dataset is a real mapping rather than another stub — unlike most sources ruled at audit-envelope-phase4. `dwintel_dl_snapshot_dt` is replication time and is EXCLUDED under the standing CAPTURE_DATE rule. Note the split: the ServiceNow columns are authorship, the dwintel ones are capture, and only the first kind is envelope. (e) Local extensions visible on this one view: `u_hash`, `u_discovery_source` (the `u_` class) and a company scoped-app data-destruction column (the `x_<scope>_` class). Both classes were predicted by the item; this confirms them on a table we would actually ingest. Mechanism only — GUID values, the scope name, database and host stay company-side. DONE 2026-08-09 (LAPTOP, same day it was raised). Output: knowledge/upgrade-plans/servicenow-replica-evidence.md — the INSTANCE half of a pair with C10's servicenow-cmdb-analysis.md (the vendor-doc BASELINE half), cross-linked both ways. All three clauses delivered. Clause (1): the nine-table join spine and a per-column map marking which columns the TOM gates already assume and which are new. Clause (2): the V_-prefix rule now has evidence behind it (no exception observed) plus the observed view inventory by family, recorded WITH its limits — the navigator was cut at both ends, and V_SYS_USER_GROUP / V_SYS_CHOICE are known present from the query rather than from the tree. Clause (3) ruled: cmdb_rel_ci + cmdb_rel_type ARE in the pull, the other seven cmdb_rel_* views are NOT (they are ServiceNow's own governance and UI machinery for maintaining edges, not the edges), and a three-ring scope is proposed for the gate to rule. FOUR FINDINGS WORTH THE ITEM. (a) The item's own premise needed correcting: these are NOT all stock tables. The two at the centre of what G35 needs — x_<scope>_cmdb_tom_main and tom_roles — are a company SCOPED APP with no vendor baseline at all, so the public-doc leg cannot cover them and G35 is reasoning about a surface the vendor has never described. (b) The SEAL ids sit on cmdb_ci_service_discovered (CSDM Application Service), NOT on cmdb_ci_business_app — and u_seal_deployment_id sits beside u_seal_application_id. The source keys application and deployment separately where DryDocs has one concept, which meets the trigger condition C10's gate-bound candidate #1 was deferred on; that candidate is annotated RE-OPENED rather than acted on. (c) G35 §E4's premise changes: it assumed the inherited-from parent CI is estate data DryDocs does not have, and the parent is cmdb_ci in the SAME replica, so E4 is now a modelling choice rather than an availability constraint. (d) A tension for §B6 — as sampled, the TOM row names a GROUP (sys_user_group), never a person, which is recorded as a limit of one report rather than a conclusion and is open question 1. Also corrected the standing evidence note on cmdb_rel_type: the vendor baseline is parent_descriptor + child_descriptor as TWO columns with name being their "A::B" concatenation, so read the columns and do NOT split name on '::'. Registered ServiceNow in reference/REGISTRY.yaml as a source-platform with the public-docs source_url, and recorded on the snowflake entry the non-obvious fact that Snowflake is already live as the replica CARRIER (the reference/platforms README said "future placeholder"). NOTHING ACTIVATED, as the item required: no source row written to config/source-registry.yaml, no loader, no gate signed. The ring-1 dataset rows are DRAFTED IN THE DOCUMENT with confirmed: false rather than pasted into the registry — deliberate, because the registry is an enforcement surface and the pull scope is a gate decision, so the gate should approve a recommendation instead of striking rows. Six open questions carried, three of them SME-blocking. Suite green (1772 passed); the one red file, test_seal_samples.py, is the uncommitted business-application.yaml work in progress and was proven independent by stashing it.

(1) Every BaseLoader subclass declares source_id resolving to a config/source-registry.yaml id — BaseLoader carries name (e.g. controlm_jobs.v1) and source_label ('csv'|'oracle'|'agent'|'human') but NOTHING tying a loader to its registered source, so loader->source->column-ledger cannot be traversed at all. Acceptance: A `drydocs docs-verify` (name at implementer's discretion) reports one row per config/doc-source-registry.yaml entry: the declared target_db, whether that corpus is present in that database, its loaded Document/Chunk counts, and a status of loaded | missing | stale | wrong-db. `stale` = the registry's recorded sha256/captured_at no longer matches what the graph carries (the ADR 0006 §4 gate-preserving freshness rule); `wrong-db` = the corpus is present in a database OTHER than its declared target_db. Exits non-zero on any wrong-db row. Covers every corpus kind the registry admits — scraped web pages, filedrop PDFs, .msg/email extracts — because the check is registry- driven, not per-loader. A unit test drives it against a fake client.

Notes: DONE 2026-08-01 (laptop, concurrent with a desktop R-epic session — claimed in a module that session was not touching). `drydocs docs-verify` + drydocs/docs_verify.py (pure; `run(database, cypher, params)` is the only I/O seam) + 16 offline tests. Suite 1330. . THE DESIGN PROBLEM THE ITEM DID NOT KNOW ABOUT: the registry is corpus-keyed and THE GRAPH IS NOT. Only the Q13 vendor-docs loader writes `corpus_id`; bmc_docs identifies pages by repo-relative `path` and essential_graphrag writes one Document whose `doc_id` IS the corpus id. A "registry-driven, not per-loader" check (the acceptance's own words) is therefore impossible unless the registry says HOW to find each corpus — so every entry now carries `graph_locator: {match: corpus_id|doc_id|path_prefix|none, value: ...}`, guarded by a new test_doc_registry case. Teaching the verifier three loader shapes instead would have made it a per-loader registry that rots silently. . SIX STATUSES, NOT THE FOUR NAMED — two live situations cannot be described by loaded|missing|stale|wrong-db, and calling either "missing" would be a FALSE diagnosis: (a) `db-absent` — bmc-docs and bmc-controlm-utilities declare target_db `dddocs`, which schema/provisioning/01_databases.cypher HAS NEVER CREATED (it makes drydocs, ddlineage, ddcontext, ddall). That is not a load failure, it is G32's open topology ruling, so it reports and does not fail. (b) `unshaped` — jpmc-reports loaded as :DataAsset slices, never on the Document->Chunk spine; its documents are not missing, they were never documents. Only wrong-db exits non-zero, per the acceptance. . LIVE RUN — laptop, container `neo4jtest` (localhost:7687), 2026-08-01: 2 db-absent (both dddocs entries) · 1 loaded (essential-graphrag in ddcontext, 1 Document / 43 Chunks) · 2 unshaped. Exit 0. NOTE THE MACHINE: bmc-docs reports "not found in any existing database either" HERE, which is a statement about this laptop's graph, not about the corpus — the two machines hold separate graphs and git syncs neither. . Two accuracy defects in the first cut, both caught by reading the live output rather than the tests: `unshaped` said "no graph_locator declared" for entries that declared `match: none` on purpose (a ruling read as a silence), and `db-absent` short-circuited before probing, so it never reported WHERE the corpus actually is — the more useful half. Both fixed; the second is now the difference between "your target is unprovisioned" and "...and it is sitting in drydocs meanwhile". . Freshness is never silently reported as fresh: the older loaders write no captured_at, and the row says "uncheckable" rather than implying a comparison that did not happen. . User-requested 2026-07-26 ("we'll need to have a registry comparison or status to check if it's loaded into the db... scraped pages - pdf - etc"). The gap is real: doc-source-registry.yaml DECLARES corpora and test_doc_registry.py enforces the declaration's shape, but nothing anywhere checks that a declared corpus was ever actually loaded, or that it landed in the database it declared. The `wrong-db` case is the one worth the non-zero exit — it is the G30 failure class at corpus granularity. MODULE CHOICE: drydocs-load, not drydocs-docmeta, because the verb lives in cli.py beside m1-verify/m3-verify and must work BEFORE the docmeta component exists (Q6). Re-home it to docmeta if that component takes over corpus state. Startable now against the corpora that exist today (bmc-docs, essential- graphrag, jpmc-reports); the multi-DB cases arrive with G32.

Q12Doc-capture scale guardrail: the web connector refuses a bulk scrape above a threshold instead of silently fetching thousands of vendor pages
drydocs-docmetaP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta
depends on: Q6

Acceptance: The web-capture entrypoint resolves its FULL target page list from the publisher's own manifest (e.g. the Author-it `toc.json`) BEFORE issuing any content request, and prints tree, page count, and estimated bytes + wall-clock at the configured delay. It REFUSES to proceed (non-zero exit, count named in the message) when the resolved count exceeds a configured threshold unless an explicit opt-in flag is passed; the threshold and the per-request delay are config values, never hardcoded literals. A `--dry-run` prints the same plan and exits 0 having fetched no content. Unit tests drive refusal-above and pass-below against a fixture manifest with NO network (the Track-1 portable rule). No capture script may land before this guard exists — Q6's acceptance carries the same clause.

Notes: User-requested 2026-07-31 after a live feasibility probe of the BMC help trees: "stop or warn the user if they try to scan that many with the script." The numbers are the argument, and they were measured, not estimated — documents.bmc.com publishes a machine-readable `toc.json` per tree, so the page count is knowable BEFORE fetching anything, which is exactly what makes a pre-flight refusal cheap and a post-hoc abort unnecessary: /supportu/INC/ (INCONTROL mainframe) = 10,912 pages ~210 MB raw; /supportu/9.0.20/ (distributed, complete) = 3,860 pages ~74 MB; /supportu/9.0.21/ (distributed, trimmed — no Utilities book) = 1,965 pages ~38 MB. Sampled pages averaged ~19 KB raw / ~6.9 KB extracted text. Two distinct harms the guard prevents, both real: hammering a third-party vendor site (robots.txt ALLOWS these paths, so politeness is entirely on us — there is no server-side backstop), and committing tens of MB of vendor copyright into a repo that is private-but-sometimes-published. A THIRD hazard motivated the request and belongs in the warning text: the operator can pick the wrong tree entirely and not notice. /supportu/INC/ is the INCONTROL MAINFRAME family (Control-D, Control-O, Control-M/Tape, JCL Verify) — its "Control-M" subtree at 40498.htm is Control-M **for z/OS** administration (CTMPLEX/Sysplex, started tasks, user exits, allocated datasets), NOT the distributed estate DryDocs models. So the pre-flight summary must name the TREE and its top-level books, not just a number — a count alone would not have caught this. . DONE 2026-08-04 (LAPTOP), and it closed in two halves rather than one build. THE REFUSAL ITSELF ALREADY EXISTED: scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py shipped it 2026-07-31 (e549f07) with --dry-run, the manifest-resolved page list, the book-by-book pre-flight naming the tree, and 14 offline tests — built ahead of this item's dependency because the capture needed it that day. What was NOT met was the acceptance's other clause, and it is the one that matters for a guardrail: "the threshold and the per-request delay are config values, never hardcoded literals". They were module constants (DEFAULT_MAX_PAGES = 600, DEFAULT_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0). . WHY THAT CLAUSE IS NOT PEDANTRY, and the reason this closed WITH Q6 rather than before it: Q6 gave the repo a SECOND door to the same third party — the component's web connector. Two doors with two literals is two different notions of "too many pages", decided by which entrypoint the operator happened to use. So the numbers moved to config/doc-capture.yaml (schema drydocs.doc-capture.v1: max_pages, delay_seconds, timeout, retries, user_agent, and the SSRF scheme allow-list), both consumers read it, and a test asserts BOTH files reference CapturePolicy so a future third door cannot quietly re-hardcode. The refusal type moved with it — one rule, one exception class, raised from one place. . The scraper's own fetch() now also enforces the scheme allow-list, which it never did: it would have followed a file:// URL in a tree definition. . Registered as an enforcement-matrix surface (config/doc-capture.yaml -> scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py + drydocs_docmeta/connectors/web.py), so the config-surface guard covers it like every other governed config file.

Q13STANDALONE repeatable vendor-docs ingestion + loader: capture -> convert -> load a NAVIGABLE spine (TOC hierarchy + page_role + abstract), taxonomy only
drydocs-loadP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta

Acceptance: A STANDALONE, REPEATABLE pipeline — its own converter, loader, cypher and `drydocs` verb, NOT a widening of load-bmc-docs (user ruling 2026-07-31: "unique enough to use a stand alone, but repeatable ingestion and loader"). It reads the capture manifest as its contract, so capture / convert / load are three re-runnable stages and re-running any of them is idempotent (MERGE on doc_id; a second full run reports zero net change). The converter strips the Author-it/ExtJS navigation chrome and emits body markdown; the loader writes :Document with doc_id, title, breadcrumb, source_url, sha256, captured_at, a deterministic `abstract` (first paragraph) and a derived `page_role`; the toc.json hierarchy loads as IN_SECTION / SUBSECTION_OF; chunks keep the established (:Chunk)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document) + NEXT_CHUNK shape. A TOC node bearing a fragment (`page` + `anchor` in the manifest) attaches to the EXISTING document as a section — it must NOT mint a second :Document. `page_role` derivation is an explicit title rule, NEVER an LLM, and the run REPORTS its unclassified count rather than defaulting pages silently (the G16 values-decide pattern). Every node carries doc_version and version_verified=false. NO meaning edges — no :ControlMUtility, no DOCUMENTS, no SEE_ALSO (Q14's gate). Counts reported per role.

Notes: Layer 1 of knowledge/upgrade-plans/vendor-docs-agent-navigation.md, and the half that needs NO ruling because it only transcribes the publisher's own structure — the taxonomy-before-ontology rule in CLAUDE.md §1. Worth doing alone: hierarchy + role + abstract already beats similarity-search-only, which is all the corpus supports today. STANDALONE, decided 2026-07-31: load-bmc-docs cannot be stretched to cover this and should not be. It consumes hand-written markdown, splits on H2, and infers a provenance TIER from heading text — a heuristic that exists only because that corpus is our lossy paraphrase. This corpus is VERBATIM throughout, so there is no tier to infer, and its real structure (TOC hierarchy, page_role, anchors) has nowhere to go in that loader's model. Two loaders with honest contracts beat one with a mode flag. REPEATABLE means the capture manifest is the contract between stages: scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py already emits it (sha256 per document, page/anchor per TOC node), so a recapture after a version bump re-runs the same convert+load with no code change. MODULE: drydocs-load beside bmc_docs.py, not drydocs-docmeta — the Q7 precedent (it must work BEFORE the docmeta component exists at Q6). The version properties are load-bearing, not bookkeeping: the capture is 9.0.20 (BMC ships NO Utilities book in the trimmed 9.0.21 publication) while the estate runs 9.0.21.300, so the graph must make "the 9.0.20 docs say X, unverified for your estate" the only answer it can produce. The config-side half of that already exists — see Q16. . DONE 2026-08-04 (LAPTOP). The pipeline itself landed 2026-07-31 in 9713118 — converter, loader, cypher, both CLI verbs, 41 offline tests — and the status was never flipped, so the repo went on advertising Q13 in next_ready for four days. This close is the VERIFICATION that flip should have carried, and it found three defects. None of them would fail a test or a load; all three are the "succeeds loudly, does nothing" reporting class this epic hit at G29, G30 and Q8. . (1) THE LOADER COULD NOT REPORT A CHANGE. vendor_docs.cypher had no WAS_GENERATED_BY provenance tail, and BaseLoader derives rows_changed by counting the edges a run attached — so it reported rows_changed=0 on a FIRST load exactly as on a no-op re-run, which makes this item's own idempotence evidence ("a second full run reports zero net change") unfalsifiable. `to_params` had been computing row_checksum all along and nothing read it. Fixed with the delta-only tail (bmc_docs / controlm_folders idiom), placed ABOVE the SUBSECTION_OF block because that block's UNWIND of an empty list drops every row at TOC depth <= 1 from the rest of the statement — the tail-ordering trap bmc_docs.cypher documents, and a test now pins the ordering. . (2) A CAPTURE IS NOT A CORPUS, and the loader wrote the wrong one. It set corpus_id to the CAPTURE id (bmc-controlm-9.0.20-utilities) while this item's own input, config/doc-source-registry.yaml, declares `graph_locator: {match: corpus_id, value: bmc-controlm-utilities}` — so Q7's `docs-verify` would have reported a fully loaded corpus as MISSING. A false negative in the one check built to stop false claims. It survived because nothing has ever run both halves together. Now every row carries BOTH: corpus_id resolved REGISTRY-DRIVEN (the entry naming this capture in its `manifest:` path — never a string transform of the capture id, and an unregistered capture refuses per docmeta invariant 1), and capture_id for which fetch produced the row. A test asserts the loaded id equals what the registry's locator searches for, so the two can no longer drift apart. . (3) doc_id WAS THE BARE TOPIC STEM ("16200"), globally unique across every capture. Author-it reuses topic ids across publications, so loading the already-registered 9.0.21 Parameters tree would have MERGEd onto the 9.0.20 Utilities documents and overwritten doc_version — silently destroying the one distinction this corpus exists to carry. doc_id and section_id are now capture-scoped. "MERGE on doc_id" stays literally true; it is doc_id that got an honest identity. Free to change because nothing is loaded anywhere yet — the build-order argument G31 makes. . Also closed the literal acceptance gap: doc_version + version_verified now ride :Chunk and :DocSection, not only :Document, so a chunk that surfaces alone in a retrieval result still carries the version caveat (Q15 returns chunk-grain rows; this is what lets those rows cite honestly). . NO LIVE RUN — ON EITHER MACHINE, and this is the honest state rather than an untested one (J18). Two independent blocks: the registry entry is `confirmed: false`, so `_gate_loader` refuses the write until an SME gate signs the doc-graph shape; and the 1016-page capture lives in the DESKTOP's data root (DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT is machine-local and git syncs none of it), so this laptop has no payload to convert. Evidence here is offline and reproducible anywhere: 60 tests over a fixture capture, including two full loads through a recording client proving the checksums are identical across runs — which is precisely the condition under which the new delta-only tail fires zero times. The graph-side count stays unproven until a machine holding the capture runs it post-gate. . Registry entries for the two remaining trees: the 9.0.21 Parameters tree in scripts/external_vendor_scrape.py has NO doc-source-registry entry, so convert refuses it by design rather than inventing a corpus id.

Q16Software -> documentation coverage: every product's docs, their residency, their load state and their blockers - including version drift
drydocs-loadP14taskp2sonnet / main
docmeta
depends on: Q13

Acceptance: (a) A COVERAGE REPORT — its own verb, `drydocs docs-coverage` — prints one row per software-registry product, WHETHER OR NOT it carries a `documentation:` block. A product with no documentation at all is the row this report exists to print: exactly one product of thirteen carries that block today, so the original documentation-block-only scope could not answer "what documentation do we hold for Airflow". Each row states the product's coverage against a ladder whose first match governs (no-corpus | unregistered-corpus | ungated | cross-db-blocked | no-locator | not-loaded | product-node-absent | loaded-no-edge | traversable-until-move | traversable | not-probed), a `blockers` list naming EVERY wall rather than only the governing one, and the currency columns: runtime `versions`, `docs_version`, every runtime version NOT in `current_for`, and a currency of current | drifted | unverified | no-docs. `cross-db-blocked` sits ABOVE every load state in the ladder, so a corpus that cannot reach an edge is never reported as merely `not-loaded`. Exits non-zero on drifted and on unregistered-corpus so a version bump or a broken pointer cannot pass unnoticed in CI — and DELIBERATELY NOT on no-corpus or cross-db-blocked, which are true statements about the world that G32 owns; failing CI on an open design ruling trains people to ignore the verb (the test_software_registry.py known-state-pin precedent). (a2) Two further sections, so nothing is counted only from the product side: one row per doc-source-registry corpus that no product names, and one row per source-registry SYSTEM with no product row — which is where Snowflake appears, being absent from the software registry entirely. (a3) The report must work with the database SWITCHED OFF: the cross-DB determination is arithmetic on two YAML fields, so a pure declaration layer answers "is an edge even POSSIBLE" without Neo4j. Graph probing is an optional injected second layer, and every graph-derived field is None (`not-probed`) when it does not run — never 0, which would be a false claim of absence. (b) The pointer reaches the GRAPH so an agent can traverse from the product it is asked about to the documentation describing it, carrying docs_version + the currency status — via the term Q14's gate confirms (DESCRIBES is already registered for :Document -> :SoftwareProduct; this may need nothing new, which is the cheapest possible answer and should be checked FIRST). Nothing is written until that gate signs. (c) `current_for` is only ever set by a human confirming a capture against a runtime version — never derived by parsing version strings. (d) The two never-silent tails are reported rather than dropped: a corpus no product declares, and a DESCRIBES edge that exists in the graph with no declaration behind it. The second is a live case, not hypothetical — see the notes. (e) The report projects a CLOSED field set — ids, enum states, integer counts, declared classification labels, repo-relative paths already committed in publishable config. It never emits `source:` / `notes:` / `source_url:` free text from either registry, because three corpora are classification Internal and their prose describes internal systems. Those entries are still counted and named by id — dropping them would itself be a silent default — but their prose never reaches the output.

Notes: User requirement 2026-07-31: "we do need a pointer to it from the software registry which should contain external-vendor version number, so that when our ingestion process moves to the next major version, we know we need to update the docs." THE CONFIG HALF IS ALREADY BUILT (same session): the `controlm` product in software-registry.yaml carries `documentation: {corpus, docs_version, current_for}` beside its existing `versions:`, and two guards in test_software_registry.py enforce that the corpus id resolves to a real doc-source-registry entry and that the drift is COMPUTABLE (both sides present and typed). The mechanism is deliberately declaration-based: when the estate moves to a new version it lands in `versions:` and is absent from `current_for`, so the gap falls out with no version-string heuristics — because "does 9.0.20 documentation still describe 9.0.21.300?" is a judgement, not a string comparison. The drift-pinning guard asserts the KNOWN state rather than failing on it: drift is a true statement about the world today (9.0.20 docs, 9.0.21.300 runtime), not a code defect, so a red suite would be dishonest. What the test prevents is the drift changing SILENTLY. The operational alarm is this item's report. Home chosen beside `versions:` on the product rather than only on the doc corpus so the comparison is LOCAL — the two numbers a human must compare sit on adjacent lines. ACCEPTANCE WIDENED 2026-08-07 (laptop) at the claim, from the user's question "when we have a tool like Apache Airflow or Snowflake and the internal runs AWS MWAA with its own reference documentation, what connects them all with a Cypher query?". Answering it exposed that (a) was scoped to products CARRYING a `documentation:` block — exactly ONE of thirteen — so the report could not have printed the Airflow row, which is the row the question was about. Widened rather than groomed as a second item: same join, same inputs, same dependency, and two half-reports over one join would grow two status vocabularies that drift. WHAT THE ANSWER TURNED OUT TO BE, recorded because it is the report's subject matter. ONE edge connects them: (:Document)-[:DESCRIBES {target_version}]->(:SoftwareProduct), status active, written by bmc_docs.cypher. There is NO Document->Vendor edge; the vendor hop rides MADE_BY. It resolves for exactly one product — 27 Documents, all controlm. Airflow is a product node with zero docs; SNOWFLAKE IS NOT IN THE SOFTWARE REGISTRY AT ALL. THE FOUR BREAKS, none of which is a bug: (1) the product->corpus pointer is YAML-only — software_registry.py's rows() never reads the `documentation:` block, which is this item's own (b); (2) the doc-source registry has NO graph representation — :DocSource is not a live label and HAS_DOCUMENT is planned with loader ~; (3) the 1016-page vendor-docs corpus is staged and gate-blocked, and vendor_docs.cypher DELIBERATELY writes no DESCRIBES edge because a relationship cannot span Neo4j databases (the Q8 finding) while the registry writes drydocs and ADR 0006 re-targets corpora to dddocs; (4) therefore NO corpus can currently declare its way to a traversable edge — target_db is constrained to {dddocs, ddcontext} by the doc-registry guard and the registry writes drydocs. G32 owns that residency ruling. THE FINDING THAT MAKES THE REPORT WORTH MORE THAN A QUERY: the one working traversal is UNREPRODUCIBLE FROM THE LEDGER. Those 27 edges come from a corpus no product declares, attributed by a hardcoded Python constant (bmc_docs.py SUBJECT_PRODUCT_ID = "controlm"), resident in a database it did not declare (bmc-docs declares dddocs, lives in drydocs). It works BECAUSE OF the residency accident G32 exists to end — so acceptance (d) requires reporting it, and the report must NOT infer the declaration from taxonomy_path, since no file maps a taxonomy path to a product id. (b) IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED behind Q14's gate, which is behind G32. The widening touches (a) only. . CLOSED 2026-08-07 (laptop) as a PARTIAL close, said out loud rather than implied. WHAT SHIPPED: `drydocs docs-coverage` + drydocs/docs_coverage.py (555 lines) + 25 tests, commit b297268 — the eleven-state first-match ladder, the `blockers` list naming every wall, the currency columns, the two tail sections (a2), the database-off declaration layer with `not-probed` rather than 0 (a3), the human-only `current_for` (c), both never-silent tails (d) and the closed field set (e). Non-zero on drifted and on unregistered-corpus only, per the acceptance. docs_coverage is classified `load` in test_module_boundary (default-deny) and listed in MODULE_MAP.md. Two follow-on commits from the same session: 0ddf880 emits the doc-governance + product-documentation fields into web/src/generated/software-registry.json and load-map.json, and 9b4cf59 builds the /software console page over them — that page is groomed as its OWN item, O56, because no item had ever claimed it. WHAT DID NOT SHIP, and is the reason this close is qualified: clause (b). No DESCRIBES edge is written from a registry declaration, because the term is Q14's gate to confirm and the residency that makes any such edge possible is G32's ruling to make — target_db is constrained to {dddocs, ddcontext} while the software registry writes drydocs, so today NO corpus can declare its way to a traversable edge. Writing one anyway would be exactly the "invent a relationship during import" failure CLAUDE.md §1 forbids. (b) therefore needs a SUCCESSOR ITEM once G32 rules; the nearest live piece of it — replacing bmc_docs.py's hardcoded SUBJECT_PRODUCT_ID with a `describes_product:` registry field — is parked in the IDEAS.md inbox as Idea-88 rather than groomed, because it touches a loader and a gated corpus behind those same two rulings. WHERE (b) IS NOW TRACKED, added 2026-08-07 on the user's ruling so it is not traceable only by this prose: G32's notes carry a CLOSE CHECKLIST whose first entry is exactly this clause — when that ruling signs, it must either mint (b)'s successor item or record (b) as declined. That puts the pickup on the item that unblocks it rather than on a reader happening to re-open this close note. VENUE (J18): the report is sample-reproducible — `drydocs docs-coverage` runs against the committed YAML with the database OFF and reproduces every declaration-layer row; the graph-probed columns in this session's run were taken on the laptop, `neo4jtest`, `drydocs` DB.
