O27QuerySpec authoring conventions: consume gated edges not raw staging columns; canonical external ref grammar; no graph element ids on external surfaces
drydocs-apiP12chorep3sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: A conventions section (drydocs_api/ docstring or a sibling doc, discoverable from query_specs.py) records three rules with rationale: (a) specs read gate-confirmed materialized edges and properties, never re-derive meaning from raw staged columns (precedence resolution lives in the loaders — the Backstage consume-the-relation-not-the-spec-field rule); (b) a canonical external ref grammar kind:namespace/name (namespace = data center where names collide across the 4 DCs) is defined for deep links and export manifests; (c) graph-internal element ids / uids never appear in URLs, manifests, or exports (documented as unstable). Existing registry specs are audited against (a) with violations fixed or flagged; a registry invariant or unit test enforces (c) where mechanical.

Notes: Groomed 2026-07-22 from assessment T2+T3 (one conventions home: two consumption rules + the ref grammar). p3 — largely codifies what O11 already does. CLOSED 2026-08-01. drydocs_api/AUTHORING.md holds the three rules with rationale, linked from query_specs.py's module docstring. The audit found the registry ALREADY compliant on all three — which was the point worth writing down: compliance was a property of careful authoring, not of the system, so nothing would have caught the first violation. Three things the work changed relative to how the item was framed: (1) The ref-grammar namespace is NOT the data center. O27 was groomed "namespace = data center where names collide across the 4 DCs"; checked against drydocs_core/schema/constraints.cypher that holds for exactly ONE node kind (ControlMHostGroup's (data_center, name) NODE KEY). ControlMJob and Condition — the two kinds most likely to appear in a deep link — are FOLDER-scoped ((folder_id, job_id) and (folder_id, name)). The rule shipped as "namespace = the declared uniqueness scope", which yields the data center where the key says so and the folder where it does not, and self-maintains because a new loader's NODE KEY already states its namespace. The doc's table is held to the constraint file by test_authoring_doc_namespace_table_matches_declared_keys — otherwise it would be a record checkable only against itself. (2) Rule (a) needed its NON-violations stated, or it would push authors into worse Cypher. explorer.conditions.v2's property join looks like a violation and is not: folder_id is a declared NODE KEY component, so the join resolves identity rather than re-deriving a relationship. Flagged not fixed — no folder->condition edge exists (conditions attach to JOBS via REQUIRES_IN_CONDITION/EMITS_OUT_CONDITION), and materialising one is an ontology decision for the gate, never a read-spec edit. (3) The element-id guard went where the RISK is, not where the item pointed. The acceptance said "a registry invariant"; the registry is hand-authored and reviewed and had zero violations, while the ephemeral path (R4) carries LLM-authored Cypher into the same export/manifest code. Guarding only the registry would have put the check on the path that cannot fail. Both paths now call one guard.ensure_no_element_ids — placed in guard.py beside ensure_read_only, which also earns it _code_regions' comment/string stripping (RETURN 'id(' as data cannot false-positive; the ADR 0003 lesson) and its lower-casing, which is what makes the check case-insensitive across ElementId( / ID( spellings. The text2cypher prompt carries the rule too: the prompt prevents, the guard catches. Zero first-party elementId uses exist repo-wide, so all of it is regression-only. Suite 1277 passed / 5 skipped (was 1272); ruff check + format clean.

O28Node status envelope for the inspector + hub health glyphs: per-source namespaced status items, derived never hand-authored (status.items pattern)
drydocs-webP12requirementp3sonnet / main
web-console

Acceptance: A documented node-status envelope — a list of per-source items {type (source-namespaced), level (info|warning|error), message, error?}, always DERIVED by a producing system, never hand-authored — is adopted as the contract for the inspector sidebar's status section and the landing hub's spoke health glyphs; at least ONE real producer is wired end-to-end (first candidate: the loader per-run WARN/reject stream attaching to its :JobRun / loaded nodes) through a QuerySpec returning that shape; the envelope doc records the Backstage status.items precedent and the rule that new sources add namespaced types, never new shapes.

Notes: Groomed 2026-07-22 from assessment T5. Requirement (future capability) — the layer-4 context-graph surface in the UI; p3 until a module needs live health. CLOSED 2026-08-01. Contract in knowledge/standards/node-status-envelope.md (Backstage status.items precedent recorded, plus the two rules: always DERIVED by a producing system, and new sources add NAMESPACED TYPES never new shapes). Producer = BaseLoader._close_run via status_items_for(), a PURE function of the run summary — which is what makes "always derived" a testable property rather than a promise (8 tests, no database). Wire = loads.status-items.v1, live end-to-end as the /loads Status frame: loader derives -> rides the :JobRun -> spec unwinds -> SpecGrid renders. UI adoption via one shared component (StatusItems + HealthGlyph) used by BOTH the Explorer inspector's status section and the landing hub's spoke glyphs, so a new producer lights both with no UI change. Four design decisions worth keeping: (1) A PROPERTY on :JobRun, not a node + relationship. A relationship type is an ontology decision that goes through the HITL gate (CLAUDE.md §1), and a derived health signal has no ontological meaning to gate — modelling it as an edge would have made every future producer's rollout gate-bound for no semantic gain. This is why O28 could close without a gate session. (2) JSON strings, not parallel lists. Neo4j cannot hold a map inside a list property; parallel lists (status_types/status_levels/...) would put the envelope's integrity in the ALIGNMENT of three lists, where one mismatched append silently mislabels an item's severity. One string per item cannot desynchronise. (3) NO all-clear item. A clean run stores an empty list, so "healthy" (a producer ran, nothing to report) stays distinguishable from "unknown" (no :JobRun at all). Collapsing them is how a dashboard ends up green because nothing is watching — the hub renders every spoke except loads as UNKNOWN today, deliberately, rather than a false green. (4) The demo inspector is fed through the SAME parser as the live path (demoStatus.ts authors JSON strings, parseStatusItems reads them), so a shape change breaks the demo surface loudly instead of leaving it rendering a format nothing produces. Scope note: the Explorer inspector's items are demo-derived because that canvas is the SYNTHESIZED demo graph — wiring it to live data needs a demo->live selection bridge that does not exist. That is graph plumbing, not contract work; the acceptance's "at least ONE real producer wired end-to-end" is met by the /loads Status frame, which is fully live. The O42 component-ledger guard fired on the new component and was answered rather than silenced: StatusItems is registered UNBOUND (26/63) because it serves two modules, so binding it to either would misstate it. Suite 1285 passed / 5 skipped; ruff clean; tsc + vite build clean.

VERIFIED on this machine: 1187 unit tests, tsc+vite build, oxlint clean; wire-level live e2e (real drydocs-api + real Neo4j + stub ADK because no agents venv here): non-admin login -> control handshake -> SSE steps arrive incrementally -> explore_ref -> runSpec 10 live rows -> export w/ cypher_sha256 manifest -> foreign session 404; headless-Edge render check of /ask?as=jdoe4821. Full LLM-in-the-loop smoke rides the agents-venv machine next session.

R6Tier-2 bounded graph-of-thoughts loop: enhance/solve controller with hard caps and the task-scoped context graph per the R1 residency ruling
drydocs-agentsP15requirementp2sonnet / main
agentic-qa
depends on: R2 R3

Acceptance: The loop engages only when Tier-1 context is insufficient; hard caps enforced (iterations <=2, next-step vote x3, fix loop <=2, per-question token budget) with a forced-solve fallback so every run terminates with an answer or an explicit "cannot answer"; the enhance branch writes ONLY the task-scoped context graph named by the R1 ruling (never drydocs / ddlineage — a test proves it); per-iteration snapshots are captured and renderable in the existing d3 graph pane; the R3 ledger records per-iteration cost so caps are tunable from data.

Notes: CLOSED 2026-08-01. tier2.py is a PURE controller taking llm/retrieve callables rather than the pipeline, so the whole loop is testable with fakes and the private coupling stays in pipeline.py; retrieval REUSES Tier 1, which is why the <=2 fix loop and the read-only pre-flight are inherited rather than reimplemented — there is exactly one path that runs Cypher, and a test pins the executed sequence. Two bounding decisions the acceptance did not settle, both stated in the module docstring: (1) a tie or unparseable vote counts as SOLVE — the failure mode of voting is not a wrong answer, it is a loop that will not stop, so ambiguity resolves toward terminating; (2) the token budget bounds EXPLORATION, not the whole run — once spent the loop stops enhancing, but evidence already bought still gets one final answer call, deliberately over budget and recorded as budget.exhausted. Refusing that last call would spend the budget gathering evidence and then discard it unanswered. With NO evidence and no budget the run makes zero calls. The R1 residency proof is STRUCTURAL, not behavioural: task_graph.py has no driver, session, database name or Cypher in it, and the test reads the source and fails if any appears. A comment saying "do not persist this" is not a control; a module with nothing to persist with is. Also fixed a real gap the acceptance named only in passing — the ledger recorded iteration=1 for EVERY call, so per-iteration cost was unavailable and the caps were untunable from data. The loop now drives the iteration counter and a test pins round 2's calls to round 2. Every cap reports whether it BIT (forced_solve, budget.exhausted), and the budget is reported on runs it never touched — a limit you can only see once it has bitten is one nobody can tune before it does. Web: rather than a second d3 copy, the deterministic placement engine moved to lib/forceLayout.ts and GraphExplorer now consumes it; the new ask/TaskGraphPane keeps its OWN visual language on purpose, because a viewer who mistakes a synthesized sub-question for a real graph node has been actively misled. Snapshots are cumulative per phase (start / iteration N / final) so any frame renders alone. Suite 1315; tsc + build clean; O42 ledger 27/64 (TaskGraphPane bound to ask/).

The gate's substance, now in the ADR: the rule is TWO-PART - (i) identity takes a neutral name, (ii) evidence/provenance vocabulary KEEPS the source's own term, so ATTRIBUTION_TIERS 'SEAL' and match_method 'seal' STAY. IF NOT EXISTS matches on NAME and would no-op. . Checked the live file - it reads `identifier: "Application ID"`, corrected at the gate sign-off, and NOT to `app_id`. That is the two-part rule in miniature: the taxonomy entry is evidence so it keeps the source's header, while the graph property is identity so it is neutral. . The sequencing inverted relative to the plan: S1 was created 2026-07-25 to rule the SHAPE before its gate authorized the graph write, and the gate ran first (07-27). S10The four :BusinessApplication MERGE loaders refuse to run against a pre-cutover graph, instead of minting the silent twin S3 argued about but never guarded
drydocs-loadP9bugp1sonnet / main
structure-remediation

Acceptance: Every loader that MERGEs `:BusinessApplication {app_id}` — seal_applications.v1, manual_seal_attribution.v1, pat_product_mapping.v1, software_registry.v1 — refuses up front when the target database holds any `:BusinessApplication` with a null `app_id`, i.e. a node a pre-S3 loader created. The refusal follows the established idiom (`batch_port_orchestrator._assert_endpoint_registries_present`): it runs BEFORE `super()._load`, so a refused run writes nothing at all — not even the :JobRun — and the message names the remediation (backfill `app_id = seal_id` on the pre-cutover nodes, or rebuild, and count first) rather than only the symptom. The count excludes `:SchemaMeta` exemplars, which carry the real label with no key and would otherwise red every load (the `_count_real_nodes` precedent). Unit tests cover both directions per loader against a fake client — refuses on a dirty graph, proceeds on a clean one — plus one test asserting the refusal happens before any write. Full suite green.

Notes: WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT AN ENHANCEMENT: it fired. The company ran `drydocs load seal_applications` against a graph that took the S3 CODE but never the S3 re-key and got `Neo.ClientError.Schema.ConstraintValidationFailed` mid-load — after partial commits, because batches commit per flush. S3's own §C2 states the mechanism exactly ("a uniqueness constraint IGNORES NULLS, so a loader still MERGEing on seal_id would silently create a SECOND node rather than fail") and seal_applications.cypher:23 repeats it in a comment, but nothing enforces it at load time. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH: graph-tests/business-application-identity TC-01 detects exactly this condition — but it is a POST-HOC verification run, so it reports the damage after the loader has done it. A detector that only runs when someone remembers to run graph-verify is not the guard the null-tolerance argument implies. SCOPED OUT: the four MATCH-only sites (batch_port_orchestrator, seal_attribution, seal_contacts, folder_attribution) do not mint twins — a MATCH miss writes nothing. They have the opposite failure (silent no-op), which their own registry-presence refusals already cover. Also out of scope: retiring the seal_id alias (§G3, a separate later gate) and any migration/backfill verb — this item REFUSES, it does not repair. Worth fixing in passing if trivial: `batch_port_orchestrator._assert_endpoint_registries_present` still counts on the pre-S3 key (`_count_real_nodes("BusinessApplication", "seal_id")`), which works only while the alias is dual-written. COMPANY-SIDE READ: this is producer payload that lands with the next port; it does not substitute for the T23 migration, which is live-state repair on their graph. BUILT 2026-08-05 (desktop). `drydocs/loaders/app_identity.py` carries `PreCutoverApplicationGuard`, mixed in BEFORE BaseLoader on all four MERGE-site loaders so its `_load` reaches the MRO first — the refusal lands ahead of `_preflight_indexes` as well as `_open_run`, which a test pins: a graph this broken should not be reported as an index problem. 15 tests in `tests/unit/test_app_identity_guard.py`, three of them parametrized across all four loaders (refuses dirty / proceeds clean / writes nothing), plus a message test (count + backfill + rebuild + the TC-03 pointer) and a COVERAGE test that re-derives the MERGE-site list from the .cypher files rather than trusting the enumeration — a fifth MERGE site added without the guard reds that test instead of passing by omission. Suite 1575 passed / 5 skipped. FIXED IN PASSING, as the item's own note anticipated: `batch_port_orchestrator`'s endpoint probe counted on the deprecated `seal_id`. It works today only because the alias is dual-written; it would have started reporting an empty registry against a good graph the day §G3 retires it. Now counts on `app_id`.

G30Decide where curated lineage lands: the writer pins drydocs while four query specs read the provisioned-but-never-written ddlineage
graph-infraP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: One ruling recorded in writing, then made true in code: either (a) drydocs_lineage.writer targets ddlineage — which means its TrustBoundaryError allowlist, DATABASE constant and the 0002-C §5 ground-truth-only tests all move with it — or (b) the four query_specs rows that declare database="ddlineage" are repointed at drydocs, and ddlineage is documented as provisioned-for-later rather than live. Whichever wins, a test asserts the writer's target and the specs' target AGREE, so a spec can never again read a database nothing writes.

Notes: Split out of G28 at its close (2026-07-26) — G28 bundled this with the naming cleanup and they are different kinds of decision: G28 was mechanical drift against an already-ruled convention, this one changes WHERE curated lineage data lives. Measured: drydocs_lineage/writer.py line 70 pins DATABASE = "drydocs" and refuses any other database (TrustBoundaryError, an allowlist — so this is a correctness and emptiness problem, not a safety one); drydocs_api/query_specs.py declares database="ddlineage" on four specs (lines 417, 540, 565, 589). Those four specs therefore query a database that is provisioned by 01_databases.cypher and written by nothing. Not urgent — the lineage writer is gate-bound anyway (its vocabulary is status: planned, so write_curated refuses a live load until the HITL gate flips it), so nothing is silently producing wrong answers today; it would bite on the first live curated write. Ties to the lineage live-load gate parked in IDEAS. DONE 2026-07-26 — RULED (b): the four specs repoint to `drydocs`; ddlineage stays provisioned + composite-aliased but documented as provisioned-for-later. The ruling is written up in ADR 0002 as a "Residency clarification" — NOT an amendment, because D1/D2 already say drydocs-lineage writes ground truth to `drydocs` and were never amended when G1 provisioning added a fourth database two days later. Each half of the codebase had followed a different source and both cited one, which is why neither looked wrong alone. Three grounds: (1) the stated reason for the DB boundary is the TRUST axis, and curated lineage is VERBATIM/GROUNDED — the same tier as the main load, so splitting it serves nothing; (2) 0002-C §5 already carries a ticked, tested "writes ground truth only" gate; (3) decisive — write_curated MATCHes :ControlMJob nodes the M3 load owns in `drydocs` and deliberately never MERGEs them (a lineage-created stub would break m3-verify's "every job has a folder"). A transaction cannot span databases, so from ddlineage those MATCHes would match nothing and every job-endpoint edge would vanish SILENTLY — an unmatched MATCH yields zero rows, not an error. Option (a) is therefore a design (a :ControlMJob proxy spine in ddlineage), not a constant flip. Deferring is also the cheap direction: ddlineage is empty, so choosing it later costs a design, not a migration. Named trigger to revisit, as an ADR amendment through the gate: the docmeta gate (ADR 0006 §b) adopted `dddocs` on the same component-per-database pattern and re-targets the bmc-docs corpus out of `drydocs` — if that proves out and lineage grows its own proxy spine, reopen. Guard: two tests in test_database_names.py — no query spec may read a database nothing writes (SPEC_DATABASES also dropped ddlineage, so pointing a spec there is now a deliberate edit), and the writer's target must equal the four specs' target. Verified load-bearing: restoring one spec to ddlineage fails 3 tests. Also corrected the user-visible UI copy that named ddlineage (module registry `backsOnto`, the Lineage SYNTHESIZED banner, route comments) — the honest reason those frames are empty is the vocabulary gate, not the database. Suite 928 -> 930.

G33Load the DryDocs code-dependency snapshot into the graph under a Project root, using the seeded-but-unused software ontology
drydocs-loadP16requirementp2fable / main
self-documentation

Acceptance: A `drydocs load-code-snapshot` verb reads the newest knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/*.json (schema depgraph-machine-first/v1) and MERGEs it idempotently into `drydocs`, so it survives the wipe-and-rebuild cycle like every other loader and is re-runnable from committed files with zero data loss (the ADR 0002 D3 stateless test). Everything hangs off an explicit (:Project {project_id:'drydocs'}) root so "is this our own code?" is one hop, and modules carry a label that CANNOT collide with the software registry's :SoftwareProduct nodes. The new node classes and relationships plus their binding to the SWO terms are registered `status: planned` and go through the HITL gate; no loader writes them until it confirms. snapshot.ps1 stays DECOUPLED — the session ritual must keep working with no database running. GATE SIGNED OFF 2026-07-27 (config/gate-prompts/self-documentation-code-graph.yaml, 36/36, 0 edits) — THIS ITEM IS NOW CLEARED TO BUILD and the acceptance is tightened to what was ruled. FIVE registrations already exist at `status: planned`, not the four this text originally named: node classes :Project and :CodeModule, edges HAS_MODULE, IMPORTS and IS_ENCODED_IN (the third added by the §E1(b) SWO ruling). Build to these rulings: (1) ONE :Project root; the snapshot's SIX scan roots are a `project` PROPERTY on :CodeModule, never sibling nodes (§B1a). (2) :CodeModule is keyed on `file_id`, the repo-relative path — the only non-colliding key (§C1a/§C4). (3) `circular` loads as a property (§C3). (4) edges carry the M2 pull-provenance fields first_seen_at / last_seen_at / last_run_id like every other loader (§D3). (5) IS_ENCODED_IN targets the already-seeded SwoClass Python, value derived from node.extension (§E1b). (6) the :CodeModule / :SoftwareProduct exclusion is a GRAPH-TEST, not a constraint — Neo4j cannot declare label mutual-exclusion (§F1). (7) the loader DISCRIMINATES ON meta.tree and REFUSES tree-mode input (§G1a) — BUILD NOTE 2026-07-27, post-sign-off review finding: the tree-mode files carry NO `meta` key AT ALL (verified: top-level keys are schema/projects/nodes/edges/stats/rels), so there is no `tree: true` to refuse on — and a naive `*.json` name-sort picks tree-this-version.json as "newest" ('t' > 'd'). A literal negative check (`meta.get('tree')` truthy → refuse) would therefore ACCEPT the tree files. Implement as a POSITIVE assertion: select `drydocs-*.json` only, require `meta` PRESENT and `meta.tree == false`, refuse loudly on anything else. The §G1(a) ruling stands; this fixes only its literal reading. SECOND selection subtlety, found LIVE at the first build run: a date-only name (drydocs-20260727.json, a one-off) sorts ordinally AFTER every timed name of the same day ('.' > '-'), so raw string sort picked the stale 12:42 capture over the 17:33 one. "Newest by filename timestamp" (§H2) must PARSE the drydocs-YYYYMMDD[-HHMM] timestamp, date-only keyed as 0000. (8) `abs_path` is DROPPED; load rel_path / file_id only (§H4). (9) a refusal must be LOUD — see the "succeeds loudly, does nothing" family. (10) register the source in config/source-registry.yaml with classification Internal-Public (§H6).

Notes: User source 2026-07-26: load the DryDocs project code snapshot under the software ontology, "which may prevent missing code fixes", plus "a way to distinguish it's for drydocs project and not the products metadata". Cheap because both halves already exist and neither is used: ontology.cypher seeds 7 SwoClass + 6 SwoProperty terms (Python, Shell, SQL, "is encoded in", "implements", "has specified data input/output", "uses platform") with ZERO consumers anywhere in the tree, and snapshot.ps1 already writes a code dependency graph every session that never enters Neo4j — it is JSON plus a viewer.html. *** THREE PREMISES IN THIS NOTE WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE (gate self-documentation-code-graph, 2026-07-27). All three came from describing the artifact without opening it, and finding them was the gate's main value: (i) it said the depgraph schema "already carries a `projects` key (=1), so the Project root matches the producer's own shape rather than inventing one". IT CARRIES SIX — drydocs, drydocs_core, drydocs_deepdoc, drydocs_lineage, drydocs_remediation, tests — and 142 of the 183 nodes declare a project that is NOT 'drydocs'. The single root was a modelling CHOICE presented as a read-off; §B1 made it a choice and ruled (a). (ii) it said "664 nodes / 86 edges at the latest". That figure belongs to tree-this-version.json, a one-off TREE-mode capture (540 files + 124 dirs, projects: ['drydocs1'], a CONTAINS relationship). The rolling dependency snapshots are 183 files / 98 edges — the real load is about a QUARTER the size this note implied. (iii) both shapes declare the SAME schema string depgraph-machine-first/v1, so a loader keying on it alone mis-reads one; §G1 ruled discrimination on meta.tree. *** TARGET IS `drydocs`, NOT dddocs, and the stated purpose is what decides it: "prevent missing code fixes" means traversing from a DryDocs module to the loader to the Control-M job it loads. That is a path query, so they must share a database — and code is not reference material ABOUT a system, it IS one, deterministically derived from source we control with no authority ambiguity. Same character as folders and jobs. The Project root is what keeps it from polluting product metadata. RE-PHASED 2026-07-26, same day, on the user's call. Groomed into phase 6 / component-topology with the marginal fit flagged rather than hidden; the user ratified it as a NEW CAPABILITY — "similar to a major version change of the snapshot ritual" — so it moved to the new phase 16 (self-documentation) and the new epic of the same name. The framing that earned the phase: the depgraph ritual's output stops being a JSON file a human reads and becomes a queryable :Project subgraph, which is a different KIND of thing, not a bigger version of the same thing. ID KEPT AS G33 DELIBERATELY. It no longer matches its epic letter, which is the lesser of two evils: ids are stable references (groom rule, git-readme §backlog id allocation) and G33 is already named in commit a37043a, which cannot be amended. Epic U is therefore the first epic whose opening item carries another letter's id — historical, not a pattern to copy. New items in this epic take U1, U2, … (T is NOT free: it is the port-turn series, e.g. docs/port-T12-*.md). Load only the LATEST snapshot as current state; the ~70 dated files (not ~20) are a time series available later if code evolution is ever wanted — §A5 scoped that out. "Do not build it" is DISCHARGED as of 2026-07-27: it meant "not before the gate", and the gate is signed. Build to the ten rulings in `acceptance`. WHAT THIS ITEM STILL DOES NOT DELIVER, stated so it is not judged against a promise it never made (§H5): the motivating query — traverse from a DryDocs module to the loader to the Control-M job it loads — needs an edge NOTHING in a dependency snapshot knows, because that mapping lives in the loaders' Cypher, not in their imports. This item lands the code subgraph and the shared database that make the join possible; the join itself is a separate Epic U item.

No graph writes, no edges: attribution is a census and Epic K still owns what it means. THE SHAPE EVERY REPORT SHARES, and the part worth reading: a row that cannot participate in the join is held OUT of the set arithmetic rather than folded into either side. A DPL-origin dataset with no registration_source_ref, a distribution with no URN, an unparseable URN — each gets its OWN counted list. Folding them into catalog_only would report gaps that do not exist; dropping them would hide real defects. That is the G25 counted-AND-listed rule extended one step. The DPL join key comes from CatalogExtract.dpl_refs(), which G42 published for exactly this consumer, rather than being re-derived here -- the rule (the catalog guid is a CATALOG id; the DPL guid lives in registration_source_ref) is not obvious and must have one home, and joining on the wrong one returns a clean-looking zero overlap. ONE DEFECT FOUND IN THIS ITEM'S OWN WORK BY THE J26 DISCIPLINE, worth carrying: the URN parser split from the RIGHT, and the module comment justified it as protecting a dotted db.schema namespace. That reasoning was WRONG -- a dot is not the separator, so left- and right-indexing agree on any well-formed URN, and the injected left-indexed split left the suite green. The real case is a COLON inside platform/namespace, where BOTH readings are wrong (last-two drops db, fields-4-5 drops the table) and neither is detectably so. drydocs-webP12taskp2sonnet / main

Acceptance: A `/software` route, registered in web/src/modules/registry.ts with `access: 'sme'` (steward + admin) and route-guarded in App.tsx, renders four tabs — Products, Vendors, Documentation coverage, Corpora — over the generated software-registry.json plus the `doc-corpus` rows of load-map.json, with exactly ONE live graph read (the registered QuerySpec `software.doc-coverage.v1`) for the in-graph column. It is a JOIN surface, not a second corpus browser: /docs already browses corpora, and the cells worth rendering are the intersections (a product whose declared corpus can never produce an edge; a product with no docs at all; corpora no product names). FOUR HONESTY RULES hold, each of which a naive build gets wrong: (1) gate state and edge state are INDEPENDENT columns, never one chip — a corpus can be both gate-blocked and permanently edge-less, and one "blocked" chip would falsely imply that signing the gate produces coverage; (2) a deliberately withheld edge renders as a RULING (teal, citing G32), never as a red gap; (3) a database the page cannot read never shows "0 documents" — an unprovisioned dddocs reads "not queried", because 0 is a false claim of absence; (4) an undeclared link is REPORTED, never inferred — the page does not derive bmc-docs -> controlm from taxonomy_path, since no file maps a taxonomy path to a product id. Ledger rows land with the code (ui-components.yaml, ui-tests.yaml and their coverage pins); `npm run build` (tsc -b) and oxlint are clean and the full suite is green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 as ALREADY DONE — the retro-groom case. software-registry.json and load-map.json were generated, drift-guarded and committed with ZERO consumers, five vendor icons sat in web/public/vendor-icons/ referenced by nothing, and no backlog item had ever claimed a page for either: the gap was invisible rather than deferred, which is precisely the state an item exists to prevent. Acceptance: A written consolidation plan (an ADR 0002 amendment or its own ADR) that answers each of these with a concrete mechanism rather than an intention: (1) HOW THE TRUST BOUNDARY SURVIVES — ADR 0002 D1 rejected the single-DB option because it commingles trust, so name the label namespace, the trust property, and the guard tests that would replace the transaction domain, and state plainly what protection is lost (the ADR's own words: multi-DB moves the guarantee "from discipline to physics", and one DB moves it back); (2) HOW ddschema's EXEMPLAR NODES COEXIST WITH drydocs' NODE KEYs — exemplars carry real labels WITHOUT the properties those keys require, which is the stated reason ddschema is its own database (G51), so this is a hard constraint conflict, not a naming collision; (3) WHAT REPLACES ddall — an enumeration of every QuerySpec, loader, and console route that names a non-default database or federates through the composite; (4) THE CONFIG CHANGE POINT — dev-environment.yaml's db-name map, and whether one map can serve both topologies so the fallback is a config switch rather than a code fork. Plan only: no provisioning, loader, or schema changes land from this item.

Notes: Worst-case contingency, groomed 2026-08-04 on the user's direction after the laptop's Neo4j Enterprise 30-day eval trial expired (2026-08-01). THE EXPIRY IS NOT THE TRIGGER and is explicitly out of scope — it is a local-testing license matter, the server keeps running, and writes were verified working after it (laptop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB: 2218 nodes, an Enterprise-only existence constraint created then dropped, six user databases online). What this plans for is Enterprise becoming genuinely unavailable — a company-side edition constraint or a cost ruling — because Community allows exactly ONE user database. That would collapse drydocs + ddlineage + ddcontext + ddschema into one store and remove the ddall composite entirely. ADR 0002 already priced this option and rejected it: "Community single DB + reliability property + :Candidate label namespace" is a listed D1 alternative, rejected because it commingles trust and "one bad query promotes noise". So this item does NOT re-open the decision — ADR 0002 stays accepted. It writes down the fallback we would otherwise have to improvise under duress, while there is time to think about it properly. The honest output may well be "consolidation costs us X and here is the sequence"; a plan that concludes the trust guarantee cannot be preserved in one database is a valid and useful result, provided it says so explicitly instead of papering over it.

G54provision.ps1 cannot run as documented on a Docker-only host: it shells out to cypher-shell on the host PATH
graph-infraP6bugp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A host running the neo4jtest container with NO local Neo4j install can provision the topology by following the script's own header. Exactly one of two resolutions: (a) the script becomes exec-aware — detect that cypher-shell is absent from the host PATH and fall back to `docker cp` of the .cypher file plus `docker exec … cypher-shell -f`, reading the container name from config/dev-environment.yaml rather than hardcoding it; or (b) the header's REQUIRES block stops presenting host cypher-shell as satisfied by "bundled in the Neo4j Docker image" — it is bundled INSIDE the image, which is not the host PATH — and documents the docker-exec invocation as the supported Docker-host form. (a) is preferred, since the header already owns the `docker run` commands and therefore already assumes Docker on this path. Either way the fix respects and states the J29 trap: do NOT pipe file content into `docker exec`; copy the file in and use `-f`, because a PowerShell 5.1 pipe injects a UTF-8 BOM that cypher-shell then rejects.

Notes: Reported 2026-08-04 from the desktop M3 reload, where the documented invocation failed and the session worked around it with docker cp + docker exec cypher-shell -f. VERIFIED at the groom (laptop, static read — no database needed): the REQUIRES block at provision.ps1:6 says "cypher-shell on PATH (bundled in the Neo4j Docker image and tarball)" while the runner at :57 invokes bare `cypher-shell -a $Uri … -f`. On a Windows host whose only Neo4j is the container, that binary is not on PATH and the script cannot complete. The BOM half of the original inbox report was WRONG and is already closed: J29's byte-scan proved every tracked .cypher and .sql is clean, and the BOM came from the PS 5.1 pipe rather than from the repo. That is exactly why the trap belongs in this item's header text — the workaround shape and the encoding standard are one lesson, and J29's own close note says this gap "stays inboxed separately". p2 rather than p1: both machines already hold working topologies, so nothing is blocked today. What is broken is the documented path for a fresh host. WORKAROUND DOCUMENTED 2026-08-04 (does NOT close this item — the script itself is unchanged): the provisioning README now carries the explicit per-file docker cp + docker exec -f block, verified end to end (laptop, neo4jtest, 2026.05.0 EE — six cypher-shell calls exit 0, smoke federates 2218/0/46). It also records the J29 pipe trap with the MEASURED cause rather than the inferred one: PS 5.1's [Console]::OutputEncoding is UTF-8 WITH a 3-byte preamble that is written ahead of the first line on stdin redirection, and neither `Get-Content -Raw`, nor $OutputEncoding (already preamble-free), nor reassigning [Console]::OutputEncoding mid-session fixes it. That measurement belongs in this item's fix.

G58Dead-script archival report: three dispositions, a stated coverage precondition, and the already-archived count
drydocs-lineageP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology
depends on: G23

Acceptance: The report G22 §E3 named as the usage axis's use case — identifying unused, deprecated code for archival and removal — ships WITH the safety properties the gate ruled, and a test proves each one. (a) COVERAGE IS STATED ON THE REPORT ITSELF, never a footnote. Every run declares its body-copy coverage, and a run over a metadata-only bundle says so in its own output. A test asserts that a report generated from a body-less fixture carries the coverage statement AND that its unreferenced rows read "no CMD_LINE reference" rather than "nothing calls it". (b) THREE DISPOSITIONS, not two, each separately counted: genuinely dead (archive and remove), MISDEPLOYED (relocate, never delete — §E1's caveat that a script may have been deployed to the wrong server), and unreferenced-but-dynamically-called (keep). A test proves the three are distinct buckets and that no candidate is silently absent from all three. (c) THE MISDEPLOYMENT BUCKET IS SCOPE-GATED: emitted only where storage_scope is `local`, because under shared storage every host sees ONE file and the finding is meaningless. Unknown scope suppresses it and COUNTS the suppression (the never-silent house rule). (d) ALREADY-ARCHIVED IS REPORTED, not only deletion candidates: scripts carrying a code-repo occurrence and NO current server-extract occurrence are counted as already archived — the progress measure toward the target state. The inverse (server occurrence, no repo occurrence) is G24's existing never_committed bucket: cross-referenced, never recomputed. (e) NO AXIS PROVES ABSENCE (§H1): every "absent on axis X" row reads as "not observed by feed X", and the active_unknown count appears in the report rather than being dropped. Full suite green.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 (laptop) from Idea-80 + Idea-82 on user instruction to groom the two TOGETHER. They are one item rather than two because they turn on the SAME argument: an absence observed by one feed is not an absence in the world. Idea-80 supplies the dispositions and the coverage precondition; Idea-82 supplies the already-archived measure and the reason it needs no new flag. WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM G23: G23 LOADS the bundle facts; this READS them. Folding the report into the loader is how a deletion-driving output gets built as a loader detail — the same distinction that keeps G55 separate from G23, and for the same reason. WHY (d) COSTS NO NEW VOCABULARY: after G22 §D2 ruled reified occurrence nodes carrying `origin`, "archived" is a SHAPE rather than a status — repo occurrence present, current server occurrence absent. That keeps it DERIVED FROM EVIDENCE rather than declared, the same move §G1 made when it put identity in the business key and made the URN a render, and it stays honest when a file comes back. DryDocs' existing word for the artifact-level fact is the TOMBSTONE (`removed_from_source_at`, the D7 sweep ruled at U13, live on :CodeModule today) — reuse the concept, and note that on :CodeModule it is a TIMESTAMP, not a status. THE SAFETY BAR IS WHY (a) AND (c) ARE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES RATHER THAN GOOD PRACTICE: the output drives DELETION, so a false positive removes live code. §H2 ruled active=true-but-unreferenced "the most dangerous false positive available" precisely because §E3's blind spot (no body copies, so script-to-script calls are invisible) is exactly what hides the caller. ONE QUESTION DELIBERATELY NOT GROOMED INTO AN ITEM: what to CALL the estate-level end state ("the production server holds only actively used code"). It is a property of the ESTATE, not of any node, so a formal graph-side term would be a vocabulary decision riding the HITL gate — and NOTHING NEEDS ONE YET. Minting an item for a decision no build depends on is how the backlog inflates. Surface it at this build if the report wants a term; the plain-English statement of the goal is L24's job and needs no gate. Explicitly DO NOT reach for the 00-header.yaml lifecycle (planned|active|deprecated|removed): that enum governs vocabulary ENTRIES (edge meanings, i.e. schema) and a script on a server is an INSTANCE — reusing the four words would put `removed` = "deleted an edge definition" and `removed` = "deleted a file off a server" in one repo, the two-things-one-spelling collision §A2 caught on `group` and J32 made a standing rule. HOME: drydocs_lineage/review.py is the lineage SME surface (CLI `drydocs lineage-review`, ported at ADR 0002-C) — the same surface §A3's signed ruling already sends same-basename multi-mount duplicates to for SME merge, so the curation ladder exists. PRIORITY NOTE: Idea-80 carried an agent-PROPOSED `prio? High` that the user never ruled. Filed p2 for coherence with its own dependency chain (G22/G23/G55 are all p2) — it cannot start before G23 regardless. Raise it if the archival drive lands before the rest of the chain. DONE 2026-08-07 (desktop, same session as G23): BUILT as drydocs_lineage/archival.py — archival_report() over the staged LineageGraph, PURE, writes nothing; findings are review material (H2/P5), surfaced as an optional section on the lineage-review page (to_html archival=..., the E3 curation-ladder surface). Every acceptance clause has its test (tests/unit/test_lineage_archival.py, 9 tests): (a) coverage stated ON the report — metadata-only runs say METADATA-ONLY RUN in their own output and dead rows read "no CMD_LINE reference observed", never a nothing-calls-it claim; (b) three distinct buckets (dead / misdeployed / dynamically_called via the who-references split: job-src rels = CMD_LINE feed, script-src rels = body-visible callers) + in_use counted, nothing silently absent; (c) misdeployment emitted ONLY under storage_scope local (all-records-local, conservative), unknown AND shared suppressed and counted; the row notes node_target polymorphism for the SME; (d) already-archived = G24 repo_only CROSS-REFERENCED from the CorroborationReport (never recomputed), never_committed likewise; no corroboration -> "archived-state not observed", not zero; (e) active_unknown passthrough (None = "registry axis not observed on this run"). The estate-level end-state TERM the notes deliberately left unminted stayed unminted — the report needed no term, plain counts suffice (L24 owns the prose goal). Suite 1698/3/5 — the 3 are the Idea-83 rich-ANSI env failures, untouched.

Notes: Groomed RETROSPECTIVELY 2026-08-02 — the work landed at e3f65af on SME direction ("update the scanner to pull all files, so that we can create the tree. the old dep snapshots can be removed this was the intent") and three committed files already cite "U9" by id. No sibling-repo change was needed: depgraph already reported tree: true, and tree mode is a strict SUPERSET. WHY THE FILTER: depgraph excludes .git and .venv but knows nothing about .gitignore, so the first whole-repo scan collected 649 ignored nodes, 386 of them .ruff_cache — ~18% of the artifact. Filtered in snapshot.ps1 rather than the loader so the committed JSON, viewer.html and the graph all show the same thing. Two Windows traps, both load-bearing: text=True translates \n to \r\n into stdin so git receives '.env\r', and in line mode git QUOTES unusual names and hands back '".env\r"' — either alone made the filter report "no git-ignored paths" against a snapshot holding 386. `-z` with binary input kills both. TWO DEFECTS INTRODUCED AND FIXED IN-RUN, both live-verified: the key FORKED (tree file_ids arrive as 'drydocs/drydocs/cli.py'; loaded raw that made two :CodeModule nodes for one file, side by side, NEITHER SWEPT — caught by asking why the count read 2410 instead of 2200), and `project` lost its meaning (it was "the scan root, one of six", a concept that existed only because of the hand-maintained list; the first fix was worse than the bug, labelling README.md a scan root). Result: 1457 :CodeModule (was 210), 458 IMPORTS, and all 45 .cypher files present as nodes for the first time. The tree is in the ARTIFACT (251 directories, 1956 CONTAINS) and deliberately NOT in the graph — U10 owns that gate. Doc drift left behind: U12.

U17DesignDoc.commit is the author's claim, not a git fact — say which one the tech-writer persona's staleness ranking uses
docsP16bugp3sonnet / main
self-documentation

Acceptance: The tech-writer persona's staleness ranking states which commit it ranks on — the commit the document CLAIMS to reflect (DesignDoc.commit, an author's assertion transcribed from the doc's own prose) or the commit that last TOUCHED the file (a git fact) — the plan records the rule WITH its reason, the query matches the rule, and the known divergence is used as the worked example: drydocs-startup-refresh-runbook carries a135a6d (2026-07-20) while its last touch is 554a4e8 (2026-07-31, Rev 5). If both readings are wanted, both are surfaced under distinct names; what may not survive is an undefined ranking.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-07 (pm) from Idea-48. Both readings are defensible — which is precisely why the undefined state is the defect — so the item is allowed to pick, provided the reason is written where the next reader finds it. Epic U rather than L: the ranking belongs to the U1-U3 code-graph review personas, even though the :DesignDoc node itself is Epic L infrastructure. DONE 2026-08-09 (desktop): RULED — the re-verify queue ranks on the CLAIM, with the git fact reported beside it and the gap between them named as its own measure. Three names now exist where one word did: claim_lag (cited commit -> HEAD, the ranking key), touch_lag (last-touching commit -> HEAD, reported, never ranked on), citation_lag (cited -> last-touching, the 'edited but never re-verified' measure). WHY THE CLAIM WINS: the mandate is the status of documents joined to the code they CLAIM to describe, and a reader trusts the citation; ranking on touch_lag answers a different question and would hide this unit's own subject, since a doc edited ten times without ever being re-checked ranks as FRESH under it. WORKED EXAMPLE, re-measured at 4ecfca0 rather than copied from the item (the divergence widened a month): drydocs-startup-refresh-runbook cites a135a6d (2026-07-20, squash day), last touched by 180f4ae (2026-08-06) — claim_lag 792, touch_lag 122, citation_lag 670. The two readings put the SAME document at opposite ends of the queue, which is the entire argument for naming the key. The item's Rev-5/554a4e8 figures were the Idea-48-era snapshot and are superseded. citation_lag ratifies the label Run 2 had to invent in-flight ('stale cite, fresh content'). THREE DEGENERATE CASES RULED rather than left to whoever writes the query: no citation -> rank unknown, never fresh, never silently substitute touch_lag; citation unreachable from HEAD -> rank maximum, because an uncheckable claim is worse than one measured far behind; and the trap — a citation can RESOLVE and still not be an ancestor. VERIFIED, and machine-dependent (J18: desktop): all five pre-squash cites Run 2 listed (807e050, ac2ea2e, 97ee81c, 24d6a4b, 0e036ff) resolve as objects here because the local archive/old-history-2026-07-20 tag keeps them alive, and NONE is an ancestor of HEAD — so `git cat-file -t` passes them on this desktop and fails them on a fresh clone, and `rev-list --count` returns a meaningless number across the disjoint history. The check must be `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. No query-pack file exists for Phase 3 (the A1-A6 pack is Phase 1's, in the tech-debt skill; the documentation skill carries no graph queries), so the plan IS the query spec and now names the exact measures and commands. New guard file tests/unit/test_code_graph_review_plan.py (5 tests): the three measures are named, the ranking key is stated, the conflation cannot return, each degenerate case is ruled, the reachability check is ancestry not object existence. All five PROVEN to fail against the original Unit 2 text before being trusted (J26) — and that exercise caught a real defect in the first draft of the conflation guard: it was line-scoped, while the original defect spanned a line break, so it would have passed the very text it exists to catch.

U19Depgraph scanner resolves no imports rooted off a directory that is its own sys.path root — scripts/ and agents/ show zero internal edges

Acceptance: The extractor resolves bare-name imports against PER-DIRECTORY sys.path roots (or an explicit alias map), and a fresh snapshot proves it on the two cases that fail today: scripts/render_board.py's seven sibling imports appear as scripts -> scripts IMPORTS edges (zero today), and the agents/ modules that import common.* / graph_qa.* against the agents/ root appear as agents -> agents edges (zero today). The first-party orphan queue is then re-counted and the review plan's 23-item figure is restated with the corrected number, since most of that queue is a false positive of this blind spot. Absolute imports from the same files must keep resolving — the U6 cross-root fix is not regressed. Venue named per J18.

Notes: Groomed 2026-08-09 from Idea-92 (persona Run 2, U-arch F1). Consequence, stated plainly: until this lands, only the PACKAGE-scoped metrics are trustworthy and the orphan queue should not be worked from. The fix belongs in the SIBLING depgraph extractor rather than in a producer wrapper — U16 is sizing exactly that in-house-vs-sibling trade, and if this can only be done here as a fourth post-processing wrapper step, that IS the trigger U16 names for forcing the call; say which one it turned out to be in the close note. DONE 2026-08-09 (desktop, neo4jtest, drydocs DB): fixed in the SIBLING extractor, which answers the question U19 was told to answer for U16 — it did NOT have to become a fourth post-processing wrapper step, so the trigger U16 names for forcing the in-house-vs-sibling call did NOT fire, and U16 stays a sizing exercise rather than a forced decision. depgraph 6ee0af6 (main, clean descendant of the a56d2fc pin, PUSHED to origin before the pin bump so the laptop can reach it — a pin naming an unpushed commit is the 2026-08-04 two-machine divergence with extra steps); producer pin bumped in config/dev-environment.yaml. THE RULE IS THE INTERPRETER'S, not a heuristic: walk up from the file while the directory is a package (__init__.py present); the first ancestor that is not is what Python puts on sys.path. That yields the script's own directory for a loose script and the non-package parent for a module inside a package, which is exactly what `python -m pkg.mod` makes importable. DESIGN CHOICE worth the record: the extra root is APPENDED after the project roots, a deliberate departure from Python, which searches the script directory FIRST. Precedence only matters when one name resolves both ways, and there the existing answer is what every committed snapshot was built from — appending makes the change purely additive, so it can create a missing edge and cannot move one that already resolved. Pinned by a test with shared.py present at both locations rather than left to a comment. BOTH ACCEPTANCE CASES VERIFIED IN THE GRAPH: scripts->scripts 0 -> 7 (all seven of render_board.py's sibling imports, plus its cross-root drydocs/plan_board.py edge); agents->agents 0 -> 20, with graph_qa/pipeline.py resolving common/__init__.py, common/specs_catalog.py and three graph_qa siblings. Whole-snapshot edges 830 -> 878 across the bump. NOT REGRESSED, checked rather than assumed: package-scope metrics are identical before and after (A3 top-15 unchanged with base.py 31, A4 0, A5 29), because packages already resolved through the repo root — the blind spot only ever lived outside them; the U6 multi-root and relative-import tests all still pass. ORPHAN QUEUE RESTATED, which was the point: 22 -> 4, with agents/ going 15 -> 0. Roughly four in five of that queue was a scanner artifact, not dead code, which is why the plan carried a do-not-work-from-it warning. All four survivors are subprocess-invoked entry points rather than dead files (knowledge/depgraph-snapshots/filter_ignored.py and probe_instrument.py, both run as scripts by snapshot.ps1; knowledge/upgrade-plans/p0-benchmark/benchmark_p0.py; scripts/extract_office_text.py), so the honest reading is ZERO first-party dead modules. The item cited 23; the plan carried 22 (15+4+3) and 22 is what was restated. Six sibling tests: the three behavioural ones proven to fail with the fix disabled, the three regression/precedence ones pass either way, which is what makes them regression tests (J26). Sibling suite 44 -> 50. Fifth instrument-change marker added to the snapshots README with the measured deltas, per the standing rule that a cross-boundary edge diff is the instrument and not growth.

G75Back-flow the two homeless Control-M parsing mechanisms the company adapter carries: BMC compact-timestamp normalization and the PL-/PG- condition-scope rule
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: Two pure functions the company's controlm_xml_adapter.py carries and the producer has NO equivalent of (verified 2026-08-11 by search, not assumed) land in drydocs_core/orchestration/controlm/ as mechanism, with the reasoning that makes each one correct written down rather than reconstructed later. (a) BMC COMPACT-TIMESTAMP NORMALIZATION. A BMC XML export stamps audit times as YYYYMMDDHHMMSS optionally suffixed with a zone token (UTC / Z / +hhmm) -- a form Neo4j datetime() cannot parse. The port must preserve all four decisions, because each one is a failure mode someone already hit: UTC and Z both normalize to Z while a NUMERIC offset is kept verbatim; an 8-digit date-only value becomes midnight; a value that is NOT the compact BMC form is HANDED THROUGH UNTOUCHED (the Oracle projections already deliver "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" and the loaders' Cypher handles the space->T itself); and anything else unparseable returns None so the loaders' existing null-guard drops ONE ROW rather than a malformed string reaching the driver and aborting the whole load. That last clause is the one worth a test of its own -- it is the difference between a bad row and a dead load. (b) CONDITION SCOPE FROM THE NAME PREFIX. PL- = LOCAL (resolves within the emitting folder's DATACENTER) and PG- = GLOBAL (resolves across DCs by name), anything else UNKNOWN. The consequence is the part that must survive: two LOCAL conditions sharing a name in different data centers are DISTINCT, so any key derived from a condition name is incomplete without the data center, and UNKNOWN must stay a returned value rather than a raised error. Both are pure, both get unit tests covering every branch including the pass-through and the None, and neither writes a graph. NO company values: the two prefixes are a documented BMC naming convention, not internal data, and the docstrings cite the capture rather than quoting a real condition or pool name. THE THIRD MECHANISM IS DISPOSITIONED, NOT BUILT. The company adapter's folder pseudo-job (JOBISN=1, so folder-level PL-<folder>-OK OUTCONDs attach to a real node instead of dangling) is a LOADER idiom and needs a graph-write context the producer does not have -- there is no producer XML-to-graph adapter to put it in. It is recorded in the reconcile-port divergence ledger with its trigger (the first producer-side loader that models folder-level conditions), per J39's disposition rule. Recording it is the deliverable; building it here would mean inventing the caller.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) at SME request, from the 19-screenshot capture of the company's three XML processors. WHY THESE TWO AND NOT THE ADAPTER: the adapter itself is the wrong base and the capture says why -- it encodes the description-token model C30 retired (INBOUND_ROUTE / OUTBOUND_ROUTE, ENV in its transfer-instance meaning, PDN_SNOW_QUEUE), it flattens the C30 scope ladder into one dict per job, and its FOLDER_ORDER_METHOD filter skips manual-order folders, which is right for a live-graph load mirroring the Oracle USER_DAILY IS NOT NULL filter and WRONG for a conformance pass, where hand-built and inactive folders are the whole drift population. That is not theoretical: the SME's own 22-job export carries no FOLDER_ORDER_METHOD, so the adapter would skip the folder entire while the lineage extractor stages all 22 jobs. So the adapter is scaffold, per the SME's framing -- "use it for the scaffold not the goal, ontology and mapping have changed" -- and these two functions are the parts that are mechanism rather than ontology, correct whatever era they came from, and currently reachable only through a module we are declining to adopt.

G76Reproduce the Quantitative Resource pool classifier producer-side as a mechanism/values twin: the grammar and the ordered rule table are ours, the pool vocabulary is not
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: A producer drydocs_core/orchestration/controlm/resource_pool.py reproducing the company classifier's MECHANISM with its vocabulary supplied as DATA. A QUANTITATIVE element on a job declares that the job consumes N slots from a named pool, and pool names follow <APP_CODE>-<SUBSYSTEM>[-<MODIFIER>]*-<KIND>; the classifier parses that into a frozen PoolClassification (name, category, app_code, subsystem, kind_suffix, secondary_label) with no I/O. THE SPLIT IS THE ITEM. The company module compiles its vocabulary into the source -- the match regexes name real target-database, controller, distribution and host tokens, and the app-code regex hardcodes a real two-letter prefix. Those are Internal and may not land in the repo. The producer copy carries the grammar, the classification contract and an EMPTY or synthetic rule table, with the real table loaded from config (the values twin lives under internal/). A test proves the module classifies correctly against a synthetic table and returns unknown for everything when the table is empty -- which is also the honest default for a repo that does not have the vocabulary. THREE PROPERTIES ARE LOAD-BEARING AND MUST SURVIVE THE REWRITE, each with its own test: (a) RULE ORDER IS CORRECTNESS, NOT STYLE. Rules are first-match-wins and one of them matches a token ANYWHERE in the name, so it must be evaluated after the more specific ones -- a pool that satisfies both reads as the earlier category. A config table must therefore be an ORDERED SEQUENCE; a mapping keyed by category would silently lose the ordering and the loss would be invisible until a misclassified pool reached the graph. (b) unknown IS A FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME, NOT AN ERROR. It returns with secondary_label None so the loader adds no label and logs a WARN, which is how misses surface in CI. Same aliases-suggest / values-decide discipline the FACT_REGISTRY next door follows. classify() always returns, including on empty and whitespace input. (c) A SPECULATIVE CATEGORY STAYS LABELLED SPECULATIVE. The company's business_app fallback has never fired -- its own comment says "None observed yet, but reserve the slot so the contract is complete". Carry the branch WITH that honesty or drop it; keeping the branch and losing the comment ships a never-observed category as though it were evidence. One inconsistency is RULED here rather than copied blind: subsystem and kind_suffix are both derived from the same token split, so a two-token name yields the same token in both fields. Decide whether that is intended and say so in the docstring; do not reproduce it silently. No graph writes; the loader-side CONSUMES_FROM_POOL edge and the five secondary labels are NOT in scope -- the labels are an ontology decision and go through the HITL gate, not a back-flow. This item ships the classifier and its contract only.

Notes: Raised 2026-08-11 (desktop) at SME request, from a complete 130-line capture the SME supplied specifically so this could be reproduced. The module has NO producer counterpart, and neither does controlm_quantitatives.py, which consumes it -- verified by path check. WHY IT IS WORTH REPRODUCING WHEN THE ADAPTER IS NOT: this one is a parser plus a lookup table, and the era problem that disqualifies the adapter does not apply -- pool-name grammar is not the description-token model and did not change at C30. It also gives a SECOND, INDEPENDENT platform signal: C32 established that a quantitative pool names the target platform separately from the job name, so the two cross-check, and a job whose name and pool disagree is a finding neither source could raise alone. That is the standing use for it, and it is why the classifier is worth having before the loader edge exists. The company docstring cites a company-side path for its design rationale, so the producer copy needs its own written warrant rather than a dangling citation.

GN1ADR 0012 — name loaders, commands and sources by the DATA, not the tool: the three-axis model and the deprecation policy
docsP6taskp1opus / main
generic-naming

Acceptance: An ADR settling the naming BEFORE any rename moves, because the alternative is renaming twice. It must carry: (a) THE MOTIVATION IN THE SME'S OWN TERMS -- company jargon entered a repo that was meant to be generic from the start (seal, pat, m1/m3 milestone ids). This is the standalone- generalization goal, not cosmetics, which is why it earns an ADR and an epic rather than a rename commit. (b) THE THREE-AXIS MODEL: the command names the SUBJECT (the data), the source registry entry carries CADENCE and ACQUISITION, and the profile is DERIVED by filtering on cadence. Today all three are collapsed into one LoadStep with hand-assigned profile tuples. (c) THE THREE BANDS: prepare / load / verify. Only the load band is source-keyed; forcing check or bootstrap into a source scheme is the same category error inverted. m1-verify and m3-verify carry the same defect as seal and pat -- milestone ids meaning nothing to a reader -- and are renamed with everything else. (d) THE SAAS QUESTION, ruled not dodged. The SME flagged ServiceNow and Jira as possible exceptions because they are widely known. The ADR should record the counter-argument and the ruling: the subject names the data (cmdb, work-items), the source id names the tool, because the SME's own CSV-to-database argument applies one level up -- if CMDB data later arrives from a different ITSM, load-servicenow is wrong and load-cmdb is still right. (e) DEPRECATION POLICY. CLI verb names are a PUBLIC CONTRACT -- company crons, scripts and the run-drydocs skill call them by name. New names ship with old ones as deprecated aliases for one port cycle, then drop. Precedent exists: cli.py already carries legacy-verb aliasing for supplements. (f) THE SOURCE-ID LAYER IS NOT A UNILATERAL PRODUCER CHANGE, and the ADR must say so or GN2 will discover it the hard way. Registry v2 is a COMPANY-CANONICAL SURFACE per the standing divergence ledger, and retired ids are governed by the D4 refusal list. Renaming pat:* source ids is a cross-repo reconciliation with new retired-id entries, not an edit. The ADR rules which of the three layers move together and which move separately. (g) The alternatives considered and rejected, with reasons -- an ADR that records only the chosen option is a design note wearing a decision's clothes.

(a) ADD the greenfield tokens: FTS_ID (watcher; vocabulary FTS1/FTS2/FTS6/FTS7 per the SME ruling carried in C30) and REC_ID (watcher; multi-valued on comma, a SOURCE-SYSTEM REFERENCE feeding dprod:inputPort -- explicitly NOT a route id). (b) DO NOT DELETE THE RETIRED ONES. The deployed estate still carries them and this parser's job is to read what is there: ENV-on-a-watcher, INBOUND_ROUTE, OUTBOUND_ROUTE and PDN_SNOW_QUEUE keep their entries plus a LIFECYCLE MARKER naming the ruling that retired them, so a legacy description parses them as a known-retired token instead of as an unregistered key. Deleting them would silently reclassify real estate data as somebody's private C16 team-local annotation, which is the one reading that governance cannot afford. (c) COMPLETENESS BECOMES ERA-AWARE: required_tokens() must not demand a retired token, so a job authored to C30 validates clean while a legacy job still validates against what it was authored to. The existing route-id exemption for non-MFTS_AGENT mechanisms stays as it is. (d) CONTACTS CHANGED CARRIER, they did not vanish. EMAIL_DL_L2 / EMAIL_DL_L3 are folder-scope documentation under C30, and EMAIL_DL_PDN is a THIRD member the FOLDER_VARIABLES table does not carry at all. Register the three at folder carrier under the C30 spellings and record that the folder-variable twins were spelled L2_EMAIL_DL_NM / L3_EMAIL_DL_NM before the rename, so a live extract authored either way still resolves. (e) RE-POINT THE STANDARD-OF-RECORD line in the docstring at the greenfield standard, with the metadata plan named as the earlier capture rather than deleted, and add a test that asserts the registry and the standard agree on the per-job-type set -- so the next ruling cannot land in prose alone. That test is the deliverable; the registry edit is the easy half. WHAT THIS MUST NOT DECIDE, stated in the acceptance so the evidence is not lost with the entries: marking the route pair retired is NOT an answer to whether the real MFT route id is the numeric form or the MFTS_RT_* string (Idea-104, still the SME's). Keep the note that records the two unreconciled shapes on whichever entry survives. Zero graph writes. Every token stays proposed; no relationship-vocabulary entry is ratified and no property term is bound.

Notes: Raised at the 2026-08-12 groom (desktop) from a cross-check of C30 (done, 2026-08-11) against the code it ruled -- not from an inbox line. WHY IT IS p1 rather than housekeeping: G68 is in next_ready and its folder-set PROFILE reads this contract, so a census run before this lands reports the retired set as missing on every conformant folder and the two new tokens as unknown; and G67's own conformance fixtures ALREADY emit "FTS_ID: FTS2", which the parser today calls unregistered. The drift is therefore live in the test tree, not hypothetical. WHY IT IS A BUG AND NOT A DESIGN QUESTION: C30 is done and SME-ruled, so nothing here decides anything -- the ruling simply never reached the module. The one judgment call is clause (b), retire-in-place versus delete, and it is made here rather than left open because the parser's stated job is reading a 4000-char field as the estate actually filled it. A greenfield standard governs what gets AUTHORED next; it cannot retroactively unwrite ~240K deployed descriptions. PORT CARE: docs/port-prompt.md records that description_tokens.py is UNION-MERGED, not wholesale -- producer holds parse_description / required_tokens / validate, the company adapter holds parse_tokens / classify_job_role, and the union survives only because the two name sets do not collide. Do not rename an exported symbol here; add to the registry and the completeness rule instead. SIBLING: G84 edits the same module and the same test file. G84Teach the description parser the DD1| sentinel — three disjoint description populations, so legacy prose stops manufacturing tokens and the compliant marker stops being reported as a defect
drydocs-coreP6taskp2sonnet / main
component-topology

Acceptance: REPRODUCED AT THE GROOM, sample-only (J18): parse_description ("DD1|DELIVERY_MECHANISM: MFTS_AGENT | FTS_ID: FTS2") returns an unparseable_segment finding FOR THE MARKER ITSELF -- the parser reports the one thing the standard makes mandatory as a defect. And parse_description("NOTE: rerun after 08:00 | contact: ops team") returns two "tokens" (NOTE, contact) with two unknown_key findings, so legacy waterfall prose is indistinguishable from a legitimate C16 team-local annotation. Guidelines section 7.5 specifies the fix; nothing implements it. (a) ONE CONSTANT, ONE PREDICATE. The marker lives in a single module-level constant and the test is startswith at position 0 -- no strip, no substring search. Section 7.5 gives both reasons and both are load-bearing: a description that QUOTES the convention in prose cannot false-positive, and startswith is the cheapest predicate available to a SQL scan over the whole estate. (b) THE PARSE RESULT CARRIES THE POPULATION -- tagged / generator-literal / untagged -- and the token grammar applies only to the tagged one. The marker itself never becomes a token and never becomes a finding. Untagged is not a defect and must not be reported as one: untagged means unread. (c) THE DIGIT IS A VERSION, NOT A TEMPLATE ID. Parse it as a version and report it, so DD1 and a future DD2 are read side by side through a grammar migration. The module must state that the marker MUST NOT select a job template -- TASKTYPE derived plus the registered JOB_ROLE token do that (section 7.2) -- because spending the version slot on template identity leaves the first grammar change with no way to announce itself. (d) COVERAGE, NOT COMPLIANCE: a helper reports tagged / total over a set of descriptions. The measure of this standard is tagged folders divided by folders, a number that grows, NOT "how much of our metadata is wrong", a number that never closes. Fewer than ten folders carry the standard today; that is a sample, not a shortfall, and the acceptance should not pretend otherwise. (e) FOLDER SCOPE IS DOCUMENTED, NOT ENFORCED. Record in the module why folder scope is preferred -- get_description() is generator-owned, so a tagged block on a GENERATED JOB is overwritten at the next regeneration and the tag does not protect it. The parser reads whatever it is given; the note exists so nobody tags jobs and loses the block. THE FENCE, and it is the reason this item is small: this implements a READ gate over free text and ratifies nothing. Exit (d) is recorded at gate email-dl-contact-point as rider section G6 with a written warrant, and THE GATE STILL RULES IT -- so the marker stays in exactly one constant and a different ruling is a one-line change, not a rewrite. Zero graph writes; every token stays proposed.

Notes: Raised at the 2026-08-12 groom (desktop) from Idea-105, which the 2026-08-11 SME design session resolved on an exit none of its three recorded ones described. THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES: two things claim the same 4000-char DESCRIPTION field -- the DPL generator's literal, which the stub plan's E1 discriminates on an EXACT match, and the company token standard captured at C29. Adding a token block to a generated object breaks E1; requiring the literal leaves the token block nowhere to go. A versioned sentinel PARTITIONS the field instead of choosing between them: the three populations become disjoint, both readers keep working, and NOTHING ALREADY DEPLOYED MIGRATES -- strictly cheaper than losing the metadata where the estate is densest, invalidating E1 on every generated object, or finding a new carrier the generator stamps. IT ALSO RETIRES C29's PROPOSED GENERATED_BY TOKEN, which is why no item mints one: absence of the tag on a literal-match description already IS the provenance signal, so a token asserting it would be a second carrier for one fact. Verified at the groom that TOKEN_REGISTRY never grew one. CONSUMER: G77 clause (a) registers a THEME token INSIDE this block and now depends on this item for that reason. COMPANY RELAY: their copy of the gate prompt is canonical-company and did not take the producer edits, so RELAY-7 carries the rider across. Nothing in this item ports on its own. SIBLING: G83 edits the same module and the same test file -- if both are open, claim them together and land one commit.

G96Control-M API-call framework the deploy/pull shell scripts can call — generic .sh, config-resolved in/out directories, calls discovered from the reference corpus (folder, job, calendar)

Acceptance: A producer-side API-call framework the Control-M shell scripts can call, built MECHANISM-ONLY (the scripts themselves — controlm_common.sh, controlm_deploy_lite.sh, controlm_folder_pull.sh with a filled controlm_deploy.cfg — are company-side; verified 2026-08-12 that this tree carries no .sh at the root and no adapters/scripts/ directory, so what lands here is the framework and the generic sample, never the instance). (a) FIRST, THE NOTE, before any code: record the convention that keeps the .sh GENERIC — an internal shell-script home and a directory that stores the API artifacts, with the INPUT and OUTPUT directories resolved from CONFIG, never hardcoded. The producer mechanism for that convention already exists and is named in the note: drydocs_core/data_root.py (remediation_incoming_dir / remediation_outgoing_dir / controlm_xml_dir under DRYDOCS_DATA_ROOT, logs under DRYDOCS_LOGDIR), with the company-side script home recorded as the vendor-namespaced scripts directory beside the adapters and the filled config staying untracked (sample committed, real values never). The note lives where the next builder looks: the framework module docstring plus a README beside the sample config. (b) THE FRAMEWORK: a Python call surface under drydocs_core/adapters/ that a generic wrapper .sh can invoke per operation, taking its endpoint/profile from config and its in/out directories from the data-root conventions, returning machine-readable results the scripts can test. Connection-profile handling is mechanism-only: shape from the corpus doc, no real endpoints, hostnames or credentials anywhere in the tree (classification boundary; secrets discipline). (c) THE DISCOVERY, in the item because the user put it there: search the knowledge graph — and where the graph does not yet hold the vendor corpus, the corpus files directly — for EXAMPLE API CALLS usable for FOLDER, JOB and CALENDAR operations, and write the candidates up as a short mechanism reference (operation, call shape, corpus source) that the framework's per-object surface is then built against. The corpus already carries controlm-api-folder-reference.md, controlm-api-job-properties.md and controlm-calendars.md plus the connection-profile and installation pages, so the search has ground truth to cite. (d) VERSION GUARDRAIL, so the framework does not assume an API the company does not run: the company orchestrator is 9.0.21.300 XML-first (the JSON/SaaS API files were demoted to conceptual reference once that was established), so the discovery step must state per candidate call whether it is available at that version, and the framework's contract must degrade honestly — an unavailable call is a reported capability gap, not a silent fallback. Tests cover the config resolution (in/out dirs from data-root, no repo-tree writes), the generic-wrapper contract, and the discovery reference existing with per-call version notes. Zero graph writes.

G98The corporate-backbone gate prompt: :Company and both HAS_BUSINESS_SEGMENT* edges execute, are constrained and are live in the graph, but were never registered in the relationship vocabulary

component-topology

Acceptance: config/gate-prompts/corporate-backbone-vocabulary.yaml drafts the rulings as confirmations to be SIGNED, never pre-decided. GATE-BOUND: drafting and rendering this page registers nothing. THE FINDING IT EXISTS FOR: (:Company {name:"JPMC"})-[:HAS_BUSINESS_SEGMENT]-> (:BusinessSegment) is MERGEd by ontology.cypher:205-232, carries a uniqueness constraint (constraints.cypher:29), is documented as THE corporate hierarchy across four .claude/skills/data-context-extractor/ files, and is live in the graph — while 10-node-classifications.yaml registers BusinessSegment and CatalogLOB and NOT Company, and no fragment registers HAS_BUSINESS_SEGMENT or its _HISTORICAL twin. NOT a regression: git log -S "Company" over the vocabulary returns nothing, so it is an M0 seed that predates the registry — there is no prior ruling to honour or overturn, which is exactly why it needs one. (a) THE LABEL: does :Company enter 10-node-classifications.yaml, and under which class? BusinessSegment is already org:FormalOrganization / prov Agent, and the note there records that the doc said FormalOrganization while the supplement comment said org:Organization — the same choice recurs here and the clause must state both readings rather than inherit one. (b) THE TWO EDGES: HAS_BUSINESS_SEGMENT and HAS_BUSINESS_SEGMENT_HISTORICAL enter as status: planned per RELATIONSHIP_GUIDE.md. The clause must ask whether the effective-dated pair is TWO edge types or ONE type discriminated by effective_to, because the seed already writes both shapes and the vocabulary would ratify whichever it is told. (c) THE SINGLETON QUESTION, which is why this is not purely clerical: :Company is a one-node class in a repo built to be generic and portable to another company (ADR 0012's standalone-generalization goal). Rule whether the label is right at all, or whether the segment backbone should hang off an existing org class — and if :Company stays, whether "JPMC" is seed data or configuration. (d) THE GUARD, separable from the ruling and buildable WITHOUT it: nothing cross-checks an edge's from_node/to_node against the registered label set — test_taxonomy_ontology_map.py checks label UNIQUENESS and test_yaml_fragments.py checks fragment KEYS, so a wholly absent endpoint raises nothing and RECONCILES_TO passes only because its endpoint happens to be registered. Record that the guard does not wait on this page. (e) PUBLISH BOUNDARY, ruled 2026-08-17 and recorded so it is not re-litigated: the source is External-PUBLIC (config/doc-source-registry.yaml#jpmc-reports — classification: External, public SEC filings / IR PDFs, source_url present), so the JPMC literals in ontology.cypher are publishable. This clause CONFIRMS that reading rather than reopening it; clause (c) is about portability, not sensitivity. NOTHING enters the vocabulary active at this gate, and nothing is transcribed to config/gate-log.md until ticked.
